When a value cannot be read, the screen says **Could not determine traffic for this period** and keeps the values it could read. Any restriction Google reports, such as sampling or privacy thresholds, appears next to the metrics, and an unknown cause is stated as unknown. Restricted data is not used for confident comparisons or advice. If Google truncated data in the selected range, the overview and the report show the reason and dates Google gave, and the period comparison is withheld.

To fix unreadable data, select **Try again** or open **Measurement health**. Switching the channel does not repair it.

## Working with report rows

Choose 50, 100 or 200 rows per page and use **Previous** and **Next** for later rows. Filters, sorting, summaries and exports apply to the page of rows on screen. Selecting a bar in a chart filters the table without changing the summary.

- A user can appear in several categories, so do not add category user counts together to get unique users.
- The same path on different hosts, and items with the same name but different IDs, stay as separate rows.
- Revenue share charts are hidden when any value is negative or unknown.

The **High traffic, low conversion** filter is a lead for investigation. It needs at least four listed pages with at least 30 sessions each, and it does not estimate lost sales. A page with no key events does not prove a tracking problem, and popular site searches do not prove missing content.

## Address groups from Opportunities

**Inspect Analytics address group** on the [Opportunities](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/opportunities/) screen opens **Landing pages** filtered to one address group, with the dates of the source data. The server reads every organic landing-page row from Google before splitting it into pages, so the whole group is matched. Query strings and trailing slashes fall into the same group; different hosts and paths with different letter case stay separate. If a source limit or data restriction prevents a complete match, the screen says so; an empty result does not prove there was no traffic. The overview keeps its property-wide scope. **Remove address group filter** returns to the full report.

## Links and exports

The report, channel, dates, breakdown, page size and position are kept in the URL, so a link or the Back button restores the same view. The exact host-and-path filter covers the listed rows only and does not merge URL variants.

**CSV** and **Export to Sheets** export the filtered rows with raw numbers. The `ga4_scope_json` column records the provider, property, dates, time zone, currency, data quality, page and filters.

## Measurement health

**Measurement health** reads the property's Admin settings: web data streams, enhanced measurement, key events and custom definitions. It changes nothing in your account. "No gaps found in the settings checked" does not prove that the tag sends data; use the linked collection checks for that. When enhanced measurement is off, none of its automatic events are active. Counts marked "at least" come from an inventory that may be incomplete.

## Quota

The collapsed quota section shows the remaining reporting tokens from the latest report response, not usage over the selected period. The standard-property limit it compares against is an assumption. **Refresh** requests the visible reports again and spends tokens.

---

# Site audit

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/site-audit/

> Crawl your site, check it against the audit rules and work through the findings by priority, with a score that shows what was measured.

The audit crawls your site with seowatcher's own crawler, which opens and reads pages one by one, and checks them against the [audit rules](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/audit-rules/). You get a score, the share of checks that could be measured, and a prioritized list of findings with fix instructions. An audit that stopped early gets no score.

## What is on the screen

**Start a new audit** has these fields:

- **Address of the site to crawl**: your project's domain is filled in already.
- **Crawl up to N pages**: at least 10, at most 10,000, default 50. If you enter more than 500, the app asks you to confirm.
- **Also measure page speed**: off by default. When on, every page is measured on mobile and desktop with Google Lighthouse. The card shows the minimum time this adds.
- **Also check outgoing links and image sizes**: after the crawl, checks whether links to other sites work and how large your image files are. At most 300 addresses are requested, and sites that block bots are skipped.

Without a [PageSpeed key](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/pagespeed-key/), speed measurement covers at most 50 pages. **Start audit** starts the crawl. The collapsed **Quotas** section below shows the current PageSpeed and URL Inspection quotas.

**Previous audits.** Each audit is listed with its date, address, status, pages crawled and finding counts. **Pages crawled** is the number of addresses actually crawled, including for failed audits, not the page limit you set. The Critical, Warning and Info columns count all stored findings, including site-wide checks; one page can have several findings. Completed audits show the page limit they ran with, or say it was not recorded. **Speed measurement requested** means speed measurement was switched on at launch, not that it finished. Failed audits show the stored reason and next step; an unknown cause is stated as unknown. On a phone, scroll the table sideways for the other columns. If more than one site has been audited in the project, a site picker appears above the list. Density means issues per hundred pages. Trend lines and change arrows appear only when stored evidence confirms the same site, page population, crawl settings and measured checks. Different or unknown scopes are shown as independent counts; change cannot be determined. While several sites are selected, the chart is hidden. **View** on a row opens the audit. The row menu has **Run again with the same settings** and **Delete audit**. Deleting also deletes the audit's pages, problems and speed measurements, and cannot be undone.

**Audit details.** At the top, **Download report** downloads a one-file HTML report and saves it in **Reports**. Below it, yellow warnings appear when needed (see below). Then comes the score card.

**Score card.** It shows these things.

- In the middle, the **Site score** and a rating word beside it: **Excellent**, **Good**, **Average** or **Poor**.
- Below it, a coverage line: "Score based on the 142 checks that were measured. 38 checks could not be measured." The question mark beside it explains how the score is worked out.
- A one-sentence verdict. If the score is held at a limit, it says why.
- **URLs found: N, crawled: M**. How many addresses the crawl found on the site and how many it opened. If the audit stopped at the page limit you chose, a note says "The audit was limited to N pages; the site may have more pages." The score still applies to the pages crawled.
- Lines for heavy categories that could not be measured. For example "Speed not measured: the PageSpeed quota ran out".
- Four counters: **Critical issues**, **Improvements** (warnings and info), **Checks passed** and **Not measured**.
- **Category scores**: Crawling, Content, Indexing, Speed, Security, Accessibility, Social and structured data. The lowest is at the top. If you click a category, the **Checks** tab opens on that category. A category nothing could be measured in says "Not measured". One that was partly measured says "Partial data".
- **Score history**: the scores of the latest audits of the same site. It appears once two audits have a score. Grey bars are partial scores. Audits that got no score are not on the chart, and a line below says how many there are.

**Tabs.**

- **To-do (N)**: the jobs, starting with the one that adds the most points. Each job shows the points you would gain, a "Small task", "Medium task" or "Large task" label and a **How to fix it** box. If Search Console is connected, the order also takes the clicks of the affected pages into account.
- **Checks (N)**: every check, by category. Each shows as passed, failed or not measured. For those not measured, the reason is written.
- **Instant data**: site-level facts beyond individual pages, such as the SSL certificate, domain registration, DNS and a preview of the site.
- **Pages with issues (N)**: groups the problems. Open a card to see the cause, the affected addresses and the **How to fix it** box. You can search the addresses.
- **Pages (N)**: every page that was crawled. Quick filters: **Blocked from indexing**, **Slow** (more than 1 second), **Missing alt text**, **Not in sitemap**.
- **Index status**: Google's answer for each page. It is covered in its own guide. If the audited site does not belong to the project's Search Console property, this tab does not show Google data and the screen explains why.
- **Speed (N)**: appears only if speed measurement was on. If some pages could not be measured, the number is written like "10/12".

The **Export** menu at the top right exports the open tab as **Export to Sheets**, **CSV** or **JSON**. With a filter on, only the visible rows are exported.

## The three states of the score

**Full score.** When most of the checks were measured, it comes with a rating word. Read the score by these ranges: 90 and above is Excellent, 70 and above Good, 50 and above Average, below that Poor.

**Partial score.** If the share of measured checks falls below 70 percent, the score is partial. It is also partial if fewer than half the checks in Crawling, Indexing, Content or Speed were measured. The card reads "Partial score — measurement coverage 62%", gives no rating word and is in a neutral colour. The number reflects only the checks that could be seen. No judgement, good or bad, was made about the rest. The usual reasons are these: the PageSpeed quota ran out, there is no PageSpeed key, speed measurement was off, or no index data could be fetched from Search Console.

**No score given.** In these cases the card says "Incomplete audit — no score given" in place of the score.

- The audit stopped with an error.
- The audit is still running.
- The crawl stopped early because of the site's rate limit. The issue list is incomplete, so a score would only be a guess.
- No page could be crawled. In that case the score card does not appear at all.

The findings are still shown and apply to the pages that were crawled. Run the audit again for a full score.

## When an audit fails

A failed audit states what happened, whether the cause is your site or the app, and what to do. The heading names the phase it stopped in: **URL discovery**, **crawl**, **speed test** or **results preparation**.

| What the screen says                                                                 | Whose side              | What to do                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A step did not finish in time                                                        | Most likely your site   | Try again in a few minutes. If it happens again, start with fewer pages           |
| The audit did not fit in the memory the app can use                                  | The app                 | Start again with fewer pages                                                      |
| The audit went over the processor time the app allows                                | The app                 | Start again with fewer pages                                                      |
| An error occurred while writing the results to the database                          | The app                 | Check that the disk has free space, restart the app and start the audit again     |
| The result of one step was larger than the app can store                             | The app                 | Start again with fewer pages                                                      |
| The app's internal audit engine reported an error                                    | The app                 | Choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the tray menu, then start the audit again  |
| The audit was cut off                                                                | The app                 | Make sure the app stays open and start the audit again                            |
| The install key did not reach the part that runs audits (your keys were not deleted) | The app                 | Update or restart the app, then start the audit again                             |
| The audit stopped with an unexpected error                                           | Could not be determined | Start again. If it keeps happening, download the diagnostics bundle from **Help** |

The raw error text is not shown on screen; it is included in the diagnostics bundle on [Help](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/help/).

## Yellow warnings during the crawl

- **The audit could not fully crawl this site.** The site's bot protection stopped the crawler. The results are still shown. Allow "seotracker-audit" in your firewall, or try one of the desktop crawlers the screen suggests (LibreCrawl, Screaming Frog).
- **N pages could not be fetched (network error).** The connection could not be made even on a retry. These pages were not audited and are not counted as broken. It is often temporary. Run the audit again. If it continues, check that the site opens from this computer.
- **The site rate-limited N pages.** The site said "too many requests". Those pages could not be audited. Start again after the rate limit resets.
- **The crawl stopped early because of the site's rate limit.** The wait that was asked for was longer than the audit may take. The report is incomplete and gets no score.
- **The saved PageSpeed key could not be read, so the speed test ran without a key.** The crawl results are unaffected, but speed was measured only for the first pages. Update or restart the app and start a new audit. If it happens again, save the PageSpeed key again in **Settings**.

## A practical routine

1. For the first audit, leave the page count at 50. Keep speed measurement off. It finishes in a minute or two. With speed measurement off the score can come out partial. That is normal.
2. Read the coverage line on the score card. If it says **Partial score**, the lines below it tell you why.
3. Start with the first three jobs in the **To-do** tab. They give the most points for the least effort.
4. In the **Pages with issues** tab, finish the critical problems first. Critical problems stop Google from seeing the page or visitors from reaching the site.
5. Take the list with **Export** and give it to your site administrator. You can pass the **How to fix it** box on as it is.
6. After fixing, click **Run again with the same settings**. The arrows in the **Previous audits** list and the **Score history** show what was fixed.
7. Turn on speed measurement once a week, for important pages. Each page takes about ten seconds and uses Google quota.

## How the numbers are calculated

**Score.** Each finding takes points off its own category. How much depends on how important the finding is and what share of pages it touches. The weights are: critical 40, warning 15, info 3. The site score is the weighted average of seven categories. Crawling and Indexing weigh the most, Social and structured data the least. A check that could not be measured neither raises nor lowers the score. That is why coverage is shown separately.

**Upper limits.** If there is even one problem, the score is at most 99. If there is a critical problem, it is at most 69. With 5 or more warnings it is at most 89. This way, one page blocked from indexing on a big site is not hidden under a high score. If a limit holds the score, the card says so. The "+N points" beside a job takes the limit into account too. Fixing the only critical problem lifts the whole limit. Fixing one warning while a limit is on adds very little.

**Crawl.** The app does not strain your site. It sends at most two requests at a time. If the site says "too many requests" (429), it waits. If the total wait goes over 30 minutes, the crawl stops and the audit gets no score.

**Speed measurement.** On a site of 212 pages, the whole audit took 35 minutes. About 24 of them were speed measurement. If the daily quota runs out, measuring stops, the results so far stay and the score may be partial. A problem is written in these cases:

- The main content shows later than 4 seconds (LCP).
- The content shifts more than 0.25 (CLS).
- The response to a click takes longer than 500 milliseconds (INP).
- The Lighthouse SEO score is below 90.

## Questions

**Does the audit show what Google sees?** No. The app's crawler reads the page itself. Google's answer is in the **Index status** tab.

**Why is my score stuck at 69?** There is a critical problem. The score cannot go past 69 until you fix it. The card says so.

**Why does it say "Partial score"?** A large share of the checks could not be measured. The coverage line and the lines below it tell you why. Turning on speed measurement or connecting Search Console usually raises coverage.

**Why did speed measurement stop partway?** Usually there is no PageSpeed key, or the daily quota is used up. **Settings → Google and system limits** shows which.

**How many audits run at once?** At most three. Two audits measuring speed slow each other down.

## Limits

The crawler may miss content that JavaScript adds after the page loads. An audit crawls at most 10,000 pages. Speed results are Google's lab measurements, not data from real visitors. The audit changes nothing on your site; you or your assistant make the fixes.

---

# Index status

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/index-status/

> Ask Google whether each crawled page is indexed, why not, and when Google last crawled it, within the 2,000 daily URL Inspection quota.

A site audit tells you whether a page loads, not whether Google has added it to its index. The **Index status** tab of a site audit asks Google's URL Inspection API about each crawled page and stores the answer on your computer.

Google allows 2,000 URL inspections per Search Console property per day. The app and your connected assistant share that allowance, so stored answers are reused and a page is checked again only when its answer is out of date.

## What the tab shows

**What has Google done with these pages?** This chart splits the crawled pages into three groups:

- **On Google**: indexed and able to appear in search.
- **Not indexed**: Google knows the page but did not index it.
- **Awaiting an answer**: not checked yet, or Google gave no answer.

**Summary boxes** count the pages checked, indexed, not indexed and awaiting an answer. **Pages where Google chose a different canonical** counts checked pages where Google picked a different URL from the canonical you declared. A separate box shows how many pages in this audit are still unchecked.

**Check status on Google** checks up to 25 pages per run, starting with pages never checked and then the most overdue answers. The button is disabled when Search Console is not connected, when no pages are left to check, or when the audited domain is outside the connected property. When the daily quota runs out, the tab shows "Google's daily limit of 2,000 URLs is used up" with the number of pages still waiting.

**The table** has the columns **Page**, **Status**, **Reason**, **Google-selected canonical** and **Google's last crawl**. Status is **On Google**, **Not checked**, **No answer**, **Check failed** or Google's own coverage status. Common coverage statuses:

- "Discovered - currently not indexed": Google knows the URL but has not crawled it yet.
- "Crawled - currently not indexed": Google crawled the page and chose not to index it.
- "Excluded by 'noindex' tag": the page asks to be kept out of search.
- "Blocked by robots.txt": robots.txt forbids Google from crawling it.
- "Soft 404": the page loads, but Google treats it as missing or empty.
- "URL is unknown to Google": Google has never discovered the URL.

You can download the table as CSV.

## Working through the results

1. After an audit finishes, open the tab. If many pages are **Awaiting an answer**, select **Check status on Google**. Each run covers 25 more pages, so a small site needs only a few runs.
2. Start with **Not indexed**. The **Reason** column usually tells you what to do: remove a robots.txt block, remove an unwanted noindex tag, or wait for "Discovered - currently not indexed".
3. For important pages marked "URL is unknown to Google", add them to your sitemap and submit it in Search Console. For a few of your most important pages, also use **Request indexing** in Search Console's URL Inspection tool.
4. If **Pages where Google chose a different canonical** is not zero, compare the **Google-selected canonical** column with your own. Either correct your canonical or make Google's choice the preferred URL.
5. Check again a few days later. Only out-of-date answers are requested again, so no quota is wasted.

## How the numbers are calculated

- Google says "indexed": the page counts as **On Google**.
- Google gives any other verdict ("not indexed" or undetermined): **Not indexed**.
- No answer yet: **Awaiting an answer**.

An answer goes out of date after 14 days for an indexed page and after 3 days for a page that is not indexed or returned an error. Pages never checked are always eligible. The daily limit counts the app's checks over the last 24 hours. Checks you run by hand in Search Console are not in this counter, but they do use Google's real quota.

A canonical mismatch means Google's chosen URL differs from yours, even by a trailing slash.

Two audit findings come from this tab: "Google hasn't crawled this page in a long time" when Google's last crawl is more than 90 days old, and "Google's answers for some pages are out of date" for stored answers past their age limit.

## Questions

**What does the 2,000 limit apply to?** The Search Console property. Two projects connected to the same property, and your assistant, draw from the same allowance.

**What should I do about "Discovered - currently not indexed"?** Usually nothing. Google can leave new sites' pages waiting for weeks. Links from pages Google crawls often speed it up.

**Does this tab submit pages to Google?** No. It only asks for their status. To get a page indexed, use your sitemap and **Request indexing** in Search Console.

## Limits

The answers are only as complete as what Google returns, and Google sometimes leaves fields empty. The tab checks only pages the audit crawled. At 2,000 checks a day, a 10,000-page site takes five days to cover.

---

# Reports and templates

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/reports/

> Save search and audit reports as standalone HTML files, browse the library, print to PDF and keep templates for your assistant.

**Reports** is the library of saved HTML reports for the project. A report is a fixed document: opening it does not refresh Google data, and the date it was saved is not the date its data covers.

## Create a report

- **Create search report** opens **Search performance**. Set the period, device, country and search type there, then select **Download report**.
- **Create audit report** opens **Site audit**. Pick an audit there and select **Download report**.
- **Copy report prompt** copies a prompt for Claude Code or Codex. The assistant studies the project and saves its report to this library.

Every report is saved before it downloads. If a download fails, download it again from the library. Saved reports stay readable even if a Google source is later disconnected.

**Templates** are written instructions for your assistant. They do not generate reports by themselves and do not run on a schedule.

## Browse the library

The **Most recently updated report** appears at the top with its saved summary, save time and open and download actions. It is not a current summary of the site. If a report has no summary or no recorded period, the library says so; open the document to see its dates and limits. The app never guesses a report's origin from its title or contents.

Search covers titles and saved summaries. **Last 7 days** shows files saved or updated in the last seven days. The type counts reflect the search and the **Last 7 days** filter. The number of matching reports and the project's total are shown separately.

The library loads 25 reports per page; use **Previous** and **Next** to reach older ones. The default order is last updated, so editing an old report moves it to the top. You can also sort by creation time or title. Search, type, filter, sort order and page are kept in the URL.

Reports made by older versions of the app read **Application report, type not recorded** instead of being counted as audits. The assistant skill or template that produced a report is shown where it was recorded. Size is the stored HTML; a downloaded file can be slightly larger.

## Open, download and print

A report opens in a sandboxed frame with no scripts or network access. Expand the source and save details for its origin, type, size and timestamps. A report keeps the language it was written in; to get another language or current data, create it again from its source screen.

- **Download as HTML** saves a file you can read offline or send to someone.
- **Save as PDF (print)** opens the report in a new tab for printing. If the browser blocks it, allow pop-ups for the app, or use **Open in new tab** and print from there.
- **Full screen** shows the report alone, with exit buttons above and below it.

A link to a report only works on your own installation; send the file instead. If a preview has not opened after 15 seconds, the library offers **Try again** and **Open in new tab**. If the list fails to refresh, the last loaded rows stay with a warning.

## What a search report contains

The cover shows the exact dates, the comparison period, the filters and when the report was generated. Days follow Pacific time; if Google did not report which days are final, the report says the last days were left out based on an assumed lag. The hidden-query share includes queries Google withholds for privacy and rows beyond the row limit. Query and page tables are capped, so their sums are not site totals.

The overlap section states its own period and thresholds, even when it finds nothing; a seven-day report can use a 28-day overlap window. Several pages appearing for one query do not prove lost clicks. Missing long-term or search appearance data is reported as unavailable, not as zero.

A report reads the data again when it is generated. Google can revise past figures, so a report may differ slightly from what the screen showed earlier.

## Regenerating and source identity

A search report is identified by the property, dates and filters; an audit report by its audit ID. Creating the same report again replaces the saved record, even in another language. Assistants cannot overwrite these app reports. If an assistant's report already has the same title, the new save is refused and the existing report is kept.

An audit report names the source site when the audit confirms it, and warns if it belongs to a different site than the project. Older reports are labelled as having an unverified source and date. **Open site audits** opens the audit history; it does not start an audit or create a report. An audit report also records the Search Console period, the source row limit and any stored mobile CrUX data it used.

## Limits

| Item                   | Limit            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- |
| Template name          | 80 characters    |
| Template description   | 200 characters   |
| Template instructions  | 3,000 characters |
| Templates per project  | 10               |
| Report size            | 500,000 bytes    |
| Report title           | 120 characters   |
| Report summary         | 2,500 characters |
| Reports per project    | 10,000           |
| Storage across install | 5 GB             |

Deleting a template keeps the reports made with it.

---

# Project context

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/project-context/

> Write down what the business sells, its goal and its key pages, so you and a connected assistant work from the same notes.

Project context is a set of notes about one project. The app stores them locally and does not verify them. A connected assistant can read and edit them through MCP, but only if it chooses to call the project context tool.

## Sections and limits

The four main sections are **Business overview**, **Current goal**, **Positioning** and **Writing preferences**. Each holds up to 4,000 characters and shows who last edited it and when. The top of the page shows which main sections are filled and the stored goal. **Fill the first empty section** or **Go to section** takes you to a section. **Save changes** saves only the main sections you changed.

**Competitors** and **Key pages** are optional lists you curate yourself. They do not measure rankings or conversions.

| List            | Entries | Field limits                               |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Competitors     | 100     | Domain 255, name 120, notes 500 characters |
| Key pages       | 100     | URL 2,048, topic 200, notes 500 characters |
| Custom sections | 20      | Title 120, body 4,000 characters           |

A key page's role is a label for your own use. Custom sections are created by an assistant; you can edit or remove them.

## Working with an assistant

**Draft with an agent** gives you a prompt to copy. It asks the assistant to request your approval before saving. The approval is part of the prompt only: the app's tools write as soon as they are called. The prompt becomes available once the project's identity has loaded.

If a section changes elsewhere while you are editing it, for example because an assistant saved it, the app rejects your whole save and keeps your draft. It then shows the text from when you started editing, the latest saved text and your draft. Merge them and save again. Assistants get the same protection by sending `expectedContent` with their write; older clients that omit it still work.

## Research log

The **Research log** shows the newest 20 entries from the last 90 days. Each entry holds up to 1,000 characters and is dated by the server's UTC day. Older entries drop out of the view even if nothing new is written, and a notice tells you when more entries exist in the window. The log is a recent-activity view, not a complete history.

## Source and setup

**Source and setup** counts six shared configuration signals for the project. It reports a missing signal and an unreadable one separately and ignores the optional lists. It is not an SEO score. A saved connection does not prove that Google data can be read, a saved PageSpeed key does not guarantee quota, and a recorded tool call by an assistant does not prove that it read this project.

**Refresh** reads the notes and setup again. If a background read fails, the screen keeps the stored information and your drafts and shows a warning. If you try to leave with unsaved changes, the app asks you to confirm.

---

# Settings

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/settings/

> What each Settings section controls, which choices apply to this browser or the whole install, and where project settings live instead.

**Settings** holds choices for this browser and for the whole installation. A project's name, domain, market and Google properties are not here; they are in **Project settings** for that project.

| Section                  | Scope                 | What it controls                                   |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Appearance               | This browser          | Theme (System, Light, Dark) and interface language |
| Google, Service account  | Whole installation    | Google credentials for Search Console and GA4      |
| Speed tests              | Whole installation    | PageSpeed Insights API key                         |
| Google and system limits | One project at a time | Quota and storage counters                         |
| About                    | Whole installation    | Installed version, update checks, release notes    |
| Windows                  | This computer         | Tray app preferences (Windows package only)        |

## Appearance and language

Theme and language are stored in this browser. Pick a language and select **Apply language**; moving through the options with the arrow keys does not reload the page. The interface language is separate from a project's market language, which is set in **Project settings**.

## Google credentials

The credentials apply to every project in the installation. If both a service account and an OAuth client are saved, the service account is used. Select the service account's JSON file, or paste it into the masked field, and save; the private key is never displayed again. A saved credential and a selected property do not prove that Google returns data. If a refresh fails, the last known configuration stays on screen with a **Try again** button. Setup steps are in [Connecting to Google](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/google-connection/).

Each project's Search Console and GA4 property is chosen in **Project settings → Connections**. Changing a project's domain keeps its Google binding and history. The project's country and language are defaults for saved keywords; the country filter on **Search performance** is chosen separately.

## Speed tests

Without a PageSpeed key the app measures at most 50 pages per audit, and Google may stop earlier. **Test key** sends one mobile request for example.com that does not count toward the audit counter. Details are in [PageSpeed key](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/pagespeed-key/).

## Limits

Choose a project to see its counters.

- **URL Inspection**: this app's checks for the project's Search Console property over the last 24 hours. The limit is 2,000 per property per day.
- **PageSpeed**: measurements by audits started in the last 24 hours.
- **GA4 tokens**: the remaining reporting tokens as of the last report response. The standard-property limit is an assumption.
- **Audit pages**: pages in the latest completed audit for the project's domain.
- **Reports and templates**: everything stored for the project.

A counter with old or missing data shows as unknown instead of zero.

## Updates

The app checks GitHub for a new version at most once every six hours and shows the date of the last successful check. **Check now** checks immediately. If GitHub limits or refuses the request, wait and try again; if the release source cannot be found, download the diagnostics bundle from [Help](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/help/). On Docker, **About** shows the commands that update the container.

## Windows preferences

These options exist only in the Windows package. They are saved in the tray app and are the same settings as in the tray menu:

- **Start with Windows**: starts seowatcher in the background when you sign in. If an administrator enabled it for all users, only an administrator can turn it off.
- **Install updates automatically**: downloads, verifies and installs new versions. When it is off, use **Güncelle** (Update) in the tray menu. In an install for all users, an administrator installs updates.

The tray app also checks for updates once a day on its own. If it cannot be reached, the section shows the preferences as unknown rather than off; select **Try again**. On Docker the section is informational and has no switches. Error messages for this section are listed in [Troubleshooting](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/troubleshooting/).

## Windows notifications

**Windows bildirimleri** (Windows notifications) in the tray menu is on by default. While the tray app runs, finished and failed audits from all projects and new announcements appear as Windows notifications within about 90 seconds, even when the browser is closed. Selecting a notification opens the relevant page, and several events arrive as one summary. Events from before the first start, events already shown and events that arrive while notifications are off are not shown later. New-version notifications follow the update setting. Windows Focus or Do not disturb can hide them. Nothing appears when the tray app is closed, and the feature is not available on Docker.

---

# Help

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/help/

> Check the installation's health, find fixes for common problems and download the diagnostics bundle to attach when you report an issue.

Open **Help** first when something does not work. It checks the installation, says what is missing and links to the setting that fixes it. It checks the setup only: for problems on your site use [Site audit](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/site-audit/), and for Google's view of your pages use [Index status](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/index-status/).

The interface is available in Turkish, English, German, French, Italian and Portuguese; change it under **Settings → Appearance**. The Windows tray menu is in Turkish only, so this guide gives its items in Turkish with the English meaning in brackets.

## Quick actions

- **Check status again** reruns the checks on the card below.
- **Download diagnostics bundle** downloads a file to attach to a problem report (see below).
- **Open the guide** opens this documentation on seowatcher.io.
- **seowatcher.io** opens the website, where the download page lives.
- **Release notes** opens the release notes screen (`/release-notes`).
- **Agent setup** opens the assistant connection screen.

## App health

The **App health** card checks five things: **Sign-in and access**, **Google sign-in**, **PageSpeed key**, **Runtime** and **Database**. A row that needs attention has a button to the right setting. Make the change, return and select **Check status again**. A row that could not be read is never shown as passing.

A passing card means the installation is set up. It does not mean your site is healthy or that Google data is current. The card shows the version and when it was checked. **Copy summary** copies the result as text.

**Google sign-in** stays yellow until a Google credential is saved; see [Connecting to Google](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/google-connection/). **Sign-in and access** reports a single-user install without a password; that is expected, because the app opens only on your own computer. If you expose it to a network, put your own password-protected sign-in in front of it.

## Port warning

If another program, often an old Docker copy, holds port 3001, the Windows package starts on a free port such as 3002 for that session. A yellow bar then appears at the top of every screen: "seowatcher is running on 3002 this time because another program is using 3001 (for example an old Docker copy). Google sign-in is set up for 3001; close that program and restart seowatcher." The **App health** card repeats it.

Google sign-in returns to port 3001, so it fails while the app runs on 3002. Close the program that holds 3001, then choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the tray menu. The app returns to 3001 and the bar disappears. Closing the bar only hides it in that tab.

## Projects and limits

**Projects** lists each project's Search Console and Analytics connection. **Open connections** goes to that project's settings. **Show limits** under **Google and system limits** shows the current state of Google's quotas.

## Common problems

Six expandable answers cover the most frequent issues, each with the steps and a link to the right setting:

- The page won't open, or the app isn't running
- The port is in use
- My agent can't connect (401)
- Speed measurement stops partway (429)
- No query data, empty charts
- I changed a setting and the app doesn't see it

Longer explanations are in [Troubleshooting](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/troubleshooting/).

At the bottom, shortcuts lead to the log files and the health address (`/api/health`). In the Windows package, **Günlükleri aç** (Open logs) in the tray menu opens the logs; on Docker, **Copy command** gives the log command.

## Report a problem

If the problem remains, select **Download diagnostics bundle** and attach the file to a GitHub issue. In the Windows package, **Sorunu bildir (GitHub)** (Report a problem on GitHub) in the tray menu prepares the issue in one step.

The bundle contains the version, setup checks, table row counts, the connected Google properties, and phase and error summaries for the last 25 audits. PageSpeed errors are included without page URLs. It contains no secrets: no Google tokens or keys, no PageSpeed key, no agent token and no session cookies. It does include project names, domains and Google property IDs, because problems cannot be diagnosed without them. Read the files before you send them.

## Empty or thin search data

On a site with little search traffic, Google hides many queries. The query list can be empty or show fewer clicks than the page totals; that alone does not mean the connection is broken. If data is missing, check the project's connections, the date range and the coverage note on that screen. A passing **App health** card does not validate those reports.

---

# Audit rules

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/audit-rules/

> Every rule the site audit applies, with what each finding means, the first step to fix it and the rule ID used in exports.

The audit applies 202 rules: 13 critical, 93 warnings and 96 info. Each rule ID registered in the app has exactly one row below.

- **Critical** (13 rules): Google cannot see or understand the page, or visitors cannot reach the site. Fix these first.
- **Warning** (64 rules in the Warning table, 29 under Additional checks): issues that gradually cost rankings and clicks.
- **Info** (62 rules in the Info table, 34 under Additional checks): smaller improvements.

Severity weights the score: critical 40, warning 15, info 3, scaled by the share of pages a rule affects. See [Site audit](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/site-audit/) for how the score is calculated.

Each row gives the rule name as the app shows it, what the finding means and the first step to fix it. The finding card in the app carries the full fix text. The ID column matches the CSV export and the identifiers your assistant sees over MCP.

## Common terms

- **canonical**: a tag that names the preferred URL of a page when several addresses show the same content.
- **noindex**: a tag that hides a page from search.
- **hreflang**: the language version tag. It points to the same page in other languages.
- **meta description**: the gray summary under the title in a search result.
- **structured data** (JSON-LD): a hidden note that tells Google what the page is (a product, an article and so on). It can add extras to the search result, such as stars or an image (rich result).
- **robots.txt**: the file that tells Google which pages it may visit. A "Disallow" line forbids access.
- **sitemap**: the list of pages on your site. **lastmod**: the date the page last changed.
- **redirect**: sending visitors from one address to another.
- **user agent**: the name a browser or crawler gives itself.
- **title** (title tag): the title shown in the tab and in search. **H1**: the main heading of the page. **alt text**: a short text that says what an image shows.
- **nofollow**: a tag that says "do not follow this link". **head**: the top part of the page source.
- **LCP**: how long the main content of the page takes to appear. **CLS**: content shifting while the page loads. **INP**: how long the page takes to respond to a click.
- **Lighthouse**: Google's page-testing tool. **SSL certificate**: the document that makes your site https (a secure address).

## Critical

| Rule                                              | What it means                                                                                                      | How to fix                                                                                         | ID                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Crawler was blocked                               | Your site's bot protection stopped the crawler. Google may be blocked too.                                         | In your firewall, allow the "seotracker-audit" user agent.                                         | blocked-page                |
| Server error (5xx)                                | The page returns a server error. Google removes such pages from search.                                            | Find the error for this address in the server logs and fix it.                                     | server-error                |
| robots.txt returns a server error                 | If Google cannot read the file, it may stop crawling the site completely.                                          | Fix the error. Check that the robots.txt address opens normally.                                   | robots-txt-server-error     |
| Start URL is blocked by robots.txt                | The address the crawl starts from is forbidden in robots.txt.                                                      | If it should be crawled, delete the matching "Disallow" line.                                      | robots-txt-blocks-start-url |
| Sitemap page doesn't load                         | A page you told Google exists returns an error.                                                                    | If the page should exist, fix the error. If not, remove it from the sitemap.                       | sitemap-broken-page         |
| A file the page needs is blocked by robots.txt    | Google cannot reach the design or code file it needs to display the page.                                          | Delete the rule in robots.txt that covers these files.                                             | blocked-resource            |
| Insecure resource on a secure page                | A secure (https) page loads a file from an insecure (http) address. Browsers block this.                           | Change the file's address so it starts with https.                                                 | mixed-content-resource      |
| Canonical points to a hidden page                 | The canonical target is hidden from search (noindex), so the two signals cancel each other out.                    | Remove noindex from the target page, or make the canonical URL the page's own address.             | canonical-to-noindex        |
| Google treats the page as empty (soft 404)        | Google treats the page as "does not exist" and keeps it out of search.                                             | If the page really does not exist, return a 404 or 410 error code. If it exists, add real content. | google-soft-404             |
| Google can't crawl the page because of robots.txt | Google's answer: robots.txt blocks it.                                                                             | Find and delete the "Disallow" line in robots.txt that covers this address.                        | google-blocked-by-robots    |
| robots.txt closes the whole site to Google        | robots.txt forbids Google from crawling the home page (usually a "Disallow: /" line). Google won't crawl the site. | Delete the "Disallow: /" line, or limit it to the folders that should stay hidden.                 | robots-disallow-all         |
| http address doesn't redirect to https            | The site's http address opens without moving to the secure version. Browsers say "Not secure".                     | Turn on "Force HTTPS" in your hosting panel, or add a permanent (301) redirect.                    | no-https-redirect           |
| SSL certificate is about to expire                | The certificate expires in less than 14 days. After that, browsers open the site behind a full-page warning.       | Renew the certificate now. If renewal is automatic, find out why it didn't run.                    | ssl-expiring-very-soon      |

## Warning

| Rule                                                                   | What it means                                                                                                                  | How to fix                                                                                                                                               | ID                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Hit the rate limit (429)                                               | The site told the crawler "too many requests".                                                                                 | Raise the request limit on the server, or exempt "seotracker-audit" from the limit.                                                                      | rate-limited-page                      |
| Crawl stopped early: rate limit                                        | The crawl stopped when the wait passed 30 minutes.                                                                             | Restart the audit once the site's request limit resets.                                                                                                  | crawl-rate-limited                     |
| Broken internal link                                                   | A link on your site goes to a page that does not open.                                                                         | Point the link to the right address, or delete it.                                                                                                       | broken-internal-link                   |
| Page returns an error (4xx)                                            | The page returns an error such as "not found".                                                                                 | If the page should exist, publish it again. If not, delete the links that go to it.                                                                      | broken-page                            |
| Redirect chain                                                         | The address redirects several times before it reaches the final page.                                                          | Redirect the first address, and the links to it, straight to the final page.                                                                             | redirect-chain                         |
| Redirect loop                                                          | The address redirects to itself or in a circle.                                                                                | Follow the redirect rules and break the loop.                                                                                                            | redirect-loop                          |
| Page with no links pointing to it                                      | The page exists only in the sitemap. Google gives it little value.                                                             | Link to it from the menu, from related posts or from a category page.                                                                                    | orphan-page                            |
| Couldn't reach robots.txt                                              | The file did not respond at all.                                                                                               | Open the robots.txt address in a browser and check that it responds.                                                                                     | robots-txt-unreachable                 |
| robots.txt exceeds the 500 KiB limit                                   | Google does not read the end of the file.                                                                                      | Shorten the file.                                                                                                                                        | robots-txt-truncated                   |
| Sitemap page redirects                                                 | The sitemap has an address that redirects to another address.                                                                  | Put the final address it redirects to in the sitemap.                                                                                                    | sitemap-redirect-page                  |
| Sitemap URL is blocked by robots.txt                                   | The sitemap asks Google to crawl the address, but robots.txt forbids it.                                                       | If it should show up in search, remove the block. If not, delete it from the sitemap.                                                                    | sitemap-disallowed-page                |
| Sitemap file is too large to read                                      | The file is over the 10 MB limit.                                                                                              | Split the sitemap into parts.                                                                                                                            | sitemap-too-large                      |
| Sitemap has more than 50,000 URLs                                      | Google accepts at most 50,000 addresses in one file.                                                                           | Split the file into parts under 50,000. Join the parts with one main sitemap file.                                                                       | sitemap-too-many-urls                  |
| A sitemap file could not be read                                       | No addresses could be read from a file that robots.txt or a sitemap index points to. The details name the file and the reason. | Open the address in a browser; if it errors or redirects, publish the file at the right address. A timeout is usually temporary, so run the audit again. | sitemap-unreadable                     |
| Sitemap has a lastmod date in the future                               | The date is later than today. Google stops trusting the dates.                                                                 | Check what generates the dates.                                                                                                                          | sitemap-lastmod-future                 |
| The sitemap lists addresses on another site                            | The sitemap lists addresses on another domain. Google usually ignores them.                                                    | Publish the sitemap on the site the addresses belong to, or fix the site address in the setting that generates it.                                       | sitemap-off-host-urls                  |
| Page loads over insecure http                                          | The page is not secure (https).                                                                                                | Ask your hosting company to turn on the free SSL certificate.                                                                                            | not-https                              |
| No title tag                                                           | The page has no title tag (title).                                                                                             | Add a title that describes the topic and is specific to the page. 50-60 characters is a good length.                                                     | missing-title                          |
| No meta description                                                    | The gray summary in the search result is missing.                                                                              | Write a description that summarizes the page and makes people click.                                                                                     | missing-meta-description               |
| Images without alt text                                                | Nothing says what the images show.                                                                                             | Write a short alt text for every image that carries meaning.                                                                                             | images-missing-alt                     |
| Page has more than one title tag (<title>)                             | The page has two title tags, and Google may use either one.                                                                    | Search the page source for "title" and keep only one.                                                                                                    | multiple-titles                        |
| Page has several different meta descriptions                           | The page has two different descriptions, and Google may use either one.                                                        | Search the page source for name="description" and keep only one.                                                                                         | multiple-meta-descriptions             |
| Title tag is placeholder text                                          | The title is something like "Home" or "Untitled".                                                                              | Write your own title that describes the topic of the page.                                                                                               | placeholder-title                      |
| Duplicate title                                                        | Several pages use the same title.                                                                                              | Give each page its own title that describes its own content.                                                                                             | duplicate-title                        |
| Duplicate main heading (H1)                                            | Several pages have the same main heading.                                                                                      | Write a different H1 for each page.                                                                                                                      | duplicate-h1                           |
| Duplicate meta description                                             | Several pages use the same description.                                                                                        | Write each page its own description, or delete the repeated one.                                                                                         | duplicate-meta-description             |
| Duplicate page content                                                 | Two pages carry the same text.                                                                                                 | Choose the main page. Link the other one to it with canonical.                                                                                           | duplicate-content                      |
| Canonical declarations contradict each other                           | The HTML and the server response name different canonical URLs.                                                                | Choose one canonical URL and state it in one place only.                                                                                                 | canonical-conflict                     |
| Canonical points to a page that doesn't load                           | The canonical target returns an error.                                                                                         | Change the canonical URL to a working page, or publish the target again.                                                                                 | canonical-to-broken                    |
| Canonical points to a redirecting page                                 | The canonical target redirects to another page.                                                                                | Make the canonical URL the final page it redirects to.                                                                                                   | canonical-to-redirect                  |
| Google sees a noindex tag on the page                                  | Google's answer: it saw noindex on the page.                                                                                   | Compare the page source with what Google sees. A plugin or a template may be adding the tag.                                                             | google-blocked-by-meta                 |
| Google chose a different canonical                                     | Google did not accept your canonical URL.                                                                                      | Look at the address Google chose. Either make it the canonical URL, or make the two pages clearly different.                                             | google-chose-different-canonical       |
| Language version code (hreflang) is invalid                            | A code that does not exist was written, such as "en-UK".                                                                       | Write the right code. For the United Kingdom it is "en-GB".                                                                                              | hreflang-invalid-code                  |
| Page doesn't list itself among its language versions (hreflang)        | The page lists the other languages but not itself.                                                                             | Add the page's own address, with its own language code, to the list.                                                                                     | hreflang-missing-self                  |
| Page turns off its links with a robots directive                       | The page has turned off following its links (nofollow).                                                                        | If you want its links to be followed, delete the "nofollow" text.                                                                                        | nofollow-page                          |
| Paginated page names the first page as its canonical                   | Page 2 names page 1 as its canonical URL. Google ignores page 2.                                                               | Make each page's canonical URL its own address.                                                                                                          | paginated-canonical-to-first-page      |
| Language version isn't linked back (hreflang)                          | Page A points to B but B does not point to A.                                                                                  | Add a hreflang line to page B that points to A.                                                                                                          | hreflang-no-return-tag                 |
| Language version points to a page that doesn't load or isn't indexable | The language version it points to returns an error or is hidden from search.                                                   | Look at the address in the details. Fix it or take it off the list.                                                                                      | hreflang-target-broken                 |
| Canonical points to another domain or to http                          | The canonical URL points to another site or to an insecure (http) address.                                                     | Unless you did it on purpose, make the canonical URL the page's own https address.                                                                       | canonical-cross-host-or-http           |
| Structured data block is broken                                        | The structured data block (JSON-LD) cannot be read.                                                                            | Paste the block into a JSON checker. Usually there is an extra comma.                                                                                    | structured-data-invalid-json           |
| Crawled by Google but not indexed                                      | Google's answer: it did not find the content good enough.                                                                      | In Google's "URL Inspection Tool", check for noindex, blocked files or content that looks empty.                                                         | google-crawled-not-indexed             |
| Discovered by Google but not crawled yet                               | Google knows the address and has put it in the queue.                                                                          | Waiting is usually enough. Link to it from pages that are crawled often.                                                                                 | google-discovered-not-indexed          |
| Google found duplicate content with no canonical declared              | Google found a copy of the page and you did not set a canonical URL.                                                           | On every page in the group of copies, add a canonical that points to the version you want shown.                                                         | google-duplicate-no-canonical          |
| Google doesn't know this URL at all                                    | The address has never reached Google.                                                                                          | Add it to the sitemap and submit the sitemap to Search Console.                                                                                          | google-url-unknown                     |
| Google found errors in the structured data                             | A field is missing in the markup written for a rich result.                                                                    | Open the address in Google's Rich Results Test. It shows the missing field there.                                                                        | google-rich-results-invalid            |
| Page declares conflicting canonicals                                   | The page has more than one canonical tag.                                                                                      | Decide which one is right. Turn off the plugin that produces the other.                                                                                  | multiple-canonical-tags                |
| Page's main content loads late (LCP)                                   | The largest element arrives later than 4 seconds.                                                                              | Look at the largest element in the PageSpeed report. It is usually an image. Make it smaller and convert it to WebP.                                     | cwv-lcp-poor                           |
| Content shifts while the page loads (CLS)                              | The shift score is greater than 0.25.                                                                                          | Give images and embedded boxes a width and a height.                                                                                                     | cwv-cls-poor                           |
| Page responds slowly to clicks (INP)                                   | The response to a click takes longer than 500 milliseconds.                                                                    | Find the scripts that slow the page most. Delay them or remove them.                                                                                     | cwv-inp-poor                           |
| Low Google SEO audit score                                             | The Lighthouse SEO score is below 90.                                                                                          | Open the page in PageSpeed Insights. Look at the failed checks in the SEO section.                                                                       | lighthouse-seo-low                     |
| Site opens both with and without www                                   | Both addresses open the page and neither redirects to the other. Google sees two copies of the same content.                   | Pick one version and permanently (301) redirect the other to it.                                                                                         | www-and-apex-both-serve                |
| Missing page returns 200 instead of 404                                | An address that doesn't exist answers "OK" (200). Google treats this as a soft 404.                                            | Make your error page return a 404 status code. Its content can stay the same.                                                                            | soft-404-on-missing-page               |
| Start page HTML is larger than 2 MB                                    | Google only processes the first 2 MB of HTML and ignores the rest.                                                             | Move large embedded data into separate files. Split long lists into pages.                                                                               | html-too-large                         |
| Server is slow to send its first response (TTFB)                       | The start page's first byte arrived after more than 800 milliseconds.                                                          | Turn on page caching, find slow plugins, and use a CDN close to your visitors.                                                                           | slow-ttfb                              |
| Page blocks zooming                                                    | The viewport tag turns off zooming on phones. Visitors with poor eyesight can't enlarge the text.                              | Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag.                                                                                         | viewport-zoom-disabled                 |
| Links whose address is "javascript:"                                   | Google can't follow these links, so it can't find their pages this way.                                                        | If it goes to a page, write the real address. If it performs an action, use a button.                                                                    | javascript-href-links                  |
| Form fields without labels                                             | A screen reader can't say what belongs in the field.                                                                           | Give every field a visible label or an aria-label.                                                                                                       | form-input-without-label               |
| Page's HTML structure is too large                                     | The page has more than 1,500 HTML elements. It slows things down, especially on phones.                                        | Load hidden content only when needed. Cut unnecessary wrapper layers.                                                                                    | dom-too-large                          |
| Near-duplicate content                                                 | These pages' main content differs by only a few words. Google may pick one and not show the others.                            | Give each page content of its own, or merge the pages and add a canonical.                                                                               | near-duplicate-content                 |
| Required properties missing in structured data                         | Fields Google requires for this type (such as Product or FAQPage) are missing. No rich result appears.                         | Add the missing fields. Check the result in Google's Rich Results Test.                                                                                  | structured-data-required-props-missing |
| Analytics id on the pages doesn't match the connected property         | Visitor data is most likely going to a different Analytics property.                                                           | Replace the tag on the pages with the right id, or connect the right property in Settings.                                                               | analytics-id-mismatch                  |
| No HSTS header                                                         | The header that tells browsers "always use https for this site" isn't sent.                                                    | Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to the server response.                                                                                         | missing-hsts                           |
| SSL certificate expires in less than 30 days                           | According to public certificate logs, the certificate expires within 30 days.                                                  | Check in your hosting panel that automatic renewal is on.                                                                                                | ssl-expiring-soon                      |
| Domain expires in less than 30 days                                    | If it isn't renewed, the site and email stop. Someone else could register the domain.                                          | Renew the domain and turn on auto-renewal.                                                                                                               | domain-expiring-soon                   |

## Info

| Rule                                                             | What it means                                                                                           | How to fix                                                                                       | ID                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| Slow server response                                             | The server's first answer comes late.                                                                   | Look at server and database time. Turn on caching (keeping ready copies).                        | slow-response                             |
| Sitemap page names another page as its canonical                 | The sitemap has an address that is a copy.                                                              | Keep only canonical URLs in the sitemap.                                                         | sitemap-canonicalized-page                |
| Sitemap page is hidden from search results                       | The sitemap has a page that is hidden from search.                                                      | If it should show up in search, remove noindex. If not, delete it from the sitemap.              | sitemap-noindex-page                      |
| Page is buried deep in the site structure                        | The page is many clicks away from the home page.                                                        | Shorten the path with links from categories, menus or featured lists.                            | deep-page                                 |
| Sitemap has no lastmod dates                                     | Google does not know the last change date.                                                              | In the setting that generates the sitemap, turn on lastmod for every address.                    | sitemap-lastmod-missing                   |
| robots.txt opens some paths only to Googlebot                    | These paths are closed to other bots, so the audit didn't crawl them. Google can.                       | Nothing needs to change. If there's no reason for it, make the rule the same for all bots.       | robots-googlebot-only-paths               |
| Internal link points to a redirect                               | The link goes to an old address and redirects from there.                                               | Replace the link with the new address it redirects to.                                           | internal-link-to-redirect                 |
| Character encoding isn't declared                                | Accented and non-Latin characters may display incorrectly in some browsers.                             | Add the line meta charset="utf-8" at the start of the head section.                              | missing-charset                           |
| Page URL is too long                                             | The address is long and hard to read.                                                                   | Keep the address short and meaningful.                                                           | url-too-long                              |
| URL contains uppercase letters or underscores                    | Two separate spellings of the same page can appear.                                                     | Write addresses in lowercase with hyphens.                                                       | url-uppercase-or-underscore               |
| No H1 heading                                                    | The page has no main heading.                                                                           | Add a single H1 that describes the topic.                                                        | missing-h1                                |
| Multiple H1 headings                                             | There is more than one main heading.                                                                    | Keep a single H1. Make the others H2 or H3.                                                      | multiple-h1                               |
| Page has almost no text                                          | The crawler found no text.
