The text may be loading later with JavaScript.                               | Check in the page source whether the text shows up.                                              | thin-content                              |
| Page links nowhere else                                          | A dead-end page: it goes nowhere else.                                                                  | Add links to related pages, to the parent category or to the home page.                          | no-outgoing-links                         |
| Title is too long                                                | Google cuts off anything after 60 characters.                                                           | Shorten the title to 50-60 characters. Put the important words first.                            | title-too-long                            |
| Title is too short                                               | The title does not describe the page.                                                                   | Write a title of 30-60 characters that says what you offer.                                      | title-too-short                           |
| Meta description is too long                                     | Google cuts off anything after 160 characters.                                                          | Put the main message first and shorten it to 70-160 characters.                                  | meta-description-too-long                 |
| Meta description is too short                                    | The description gives no reason to click.                                                               | Write 70-160 characters that summarize the page.                                                 | meta-description-too-short                |
| Heading levels are skipped                                       | It jumps from H1 straight to H3.                                                                        | Use headings in order: H1, H2, H3.                                                               | heading-order-skip                        |
| No mobile viewport tag                                           | The page looks tiny on a phone.                                                                         | Add the viewport line to the head section.                                                       | missing-viewport                          |
| Page language isn't declared                                     | It does not say what language the page is in (no lang on the html tag).                                 | For an English page, write html lang="en".                                                       | missing-lang                              |
| Images have no width and height                                  | Content jumps while the page loads.                                                                     | Write the real size of the image on every img tag.                                               | images-missing-dimensions                 |
| Long text has no subheadings                                     | The long post is one single block.                                                                      | Split the text by topic. Give each section an H2 heading.                                        | no-subheadings                            |
| Image alt text is a file name                                    | The alt text is something like "IMG_1234.jpg".                                                          | In the alt text, write what is in the image.                                                     | alt-is-filename                           |
| Image alt text is too long                                       | The alt text is as long as a paragraph.                                                                 | Describe the image in one sentence. About 125 characters is enough.                              | alt-too-long                              |
| Main heading (H1) is too long                                    | The H1 is as long as a paragraph.                                                                       | Cut the H1 down to a short, one-sentence heading.                                                | h1-too-long                               |
| Internal links with no text                                      | The link has no text or only an icon.                                                                   | Add visible text or an aria-label (a name hidden for screen readers).                            | empty-anchor-text                         |
| Meaningless link text such as "Click here"                       | The link text does not say where it goes.                                                               | Replace the link text with the topic of the target page.                                         | generic-anchor-text                       |
| Too many links on the page                                       | The page has hundreds of links.                                                                         | Limit the menu and the footer to the most important pages.                                       | too-many-links                            |
| Nofollow links to your own pages                                 | A link to your own pages has nofollow.                                                                  | Delete rel="nofollow" from these links.                                                          | internal-nofollow-links                   |
| Page has no canonical tag                                        | Google guesses the canonical URL.                                                                       | Add a canonical line to the head section that points to the page's own full address.             | missing-canonical                         |
| Page is hidden from search results (noindex)                     | The page is hidden from search, on purpose or by mistake.                                               | If it should show up in search, remove noindex.                                                  | noindex-page                              |
| Page names another page as its canonical                         | The page declares itself a copy.                                                                        | If it should show up in search under its own name, make the canonical URL its own address.       | canonicalized-page                        |
| Language versions have no default (x-default)                    | There is no default version for visitors whose language does not match.                                 | Add an x-default line to the hreflang list.                                                      | hreflang-missing-x-default                |
| Google's answers for some pages are out of date                  | Stored Google answers are older than 3 or 14 days.                                                      | On the **Index status** tab, press the "Check status on Google" button.                          | stale-google-verdicts                     |
| Site has no social sharing tags (Open Graph)                     | No image or title appears when it is shared.                                                            | In the template's head section, add og:title, og:description and an og:image of 1200x630 pixels. | open-graph-missing-site                   |
| Site has no structured data                                      | A rich result cannot appear in search.                                                                  | Start with markup that fits the page type (such as Organization, Product or Article).            | structured-data-missing-site              |
| Google hasn't crawled this page in a long time                   | Google's last visit is older than 90 days.                                                              | Link to it from pages that are crawled often. Make sure the page is in the sitemap.              | google-crawl-stale                        |
| Missing pages redirect to the home page                          | An address that doesn't exist goes to the home page. Google usually treats this as a soft 404.          | Show an error page that returns 404 for missing addresses. Redirect only pages that moved.       | not-found-redirects-home                  |
| Site icon (favicon) not found                                    | Mobile search shows a generic icon next to your site's name.                                            | Upload a square icon of at least 48x48 pixels and declare it in the head section.                | missing-favicon                           |
| robots.txt doesn't point to the sitemap                          | robots.txt has no "Sitemap:" line. Bing and other crawlers find the sitemap there.                      | Add a "Sitemap:" line with the sitemap's full address at the end of the file.                    | robots-missing-sitemap-line               |
| Some AI crawlers are blocked by robots.txt                       | Bots such as GPTBot and ClaudeBot are disallowed. This is a choice. Google Search isn't affected.       | If you did it on purpose, leave it. To appear in AI answers, allow the search bots.              | ai-crawlers-blocked                       |
| No llms.txt file (optional)                                      | The file proposed for AI assistants is missing. It isn't a standard and Google doesn't use it.          | If you like, put an /llms.txt listing your key pages at the site root.                           | missing-llms-txt                          |
| Start page arrived uncompressed                                  | The page arrived without gzip or brotli compression.                                                    | Turn on compression on the server or CDN.                                                        | no-compression                            |
| Open Graph tags incomplete                                       | The title, description or image for the sharing card is missing.                                        | Add og:title, og:description and og:image together.                                              | og-incomplete                             |
| No X (Twitter) card tag                                          | On X the link may show as a plain address without a card.                                               | Add a twitter:card tag (summary_large_image) to the head section.                                | twitter-card-missing                      |
| Title tag and H1 are identical                                   | Not an error, but one of two separate chances is wasted.                                                | Write the title for the search result and the H1 for the reader on the page.                     | title-equals-h1                           |
| Title may be cut off in search results                           | The title is short, but wide letters push it past about 580 pixels.                                     | Shorten the title, or write capitalised words in normal case.                                    | title-pixel-too-wide                      |
| Unnecessary meta keywords tag                                    | Google doesn't use this tag at all.                                                                     | Remove it from the template or from your SEO plugin's settings.                                  | meta-keywords-present                     |
| Best practice: external links open in a new tab without noopener | A best-practice note. Current browsers already do this on their own.                                    | Add rel="noopener" to these links.                                                               | blank-target-without-noopener             |
| Images further down load immediately                             | More than six images below the first screen load as soon as the page opens.                             | Add loading="lazy" to them. Don't add it to the main image on the first screen.                  | images-not-lazy                           |
| Images in older formats                                          | Three or more images are JPEG, PNG or GIF with no newer-format alternative.                             | Convert the images to WebP or AVIF.                                                              | images-legacy-format                      |
| Same id on several elements                                      | Form labels and in-page links may point to the wrong element.                                           | Make every id unique. If it's only for styling, use a class.                                     | duplicate-ids                             |
| HTML elements nested too deeply                                  | The page has elements nested more than 32 levels deep.                                                  | Remove unnecessary wrapper layers from the template.                                             | dom-too-deep                              |
| Very little visible text compared with code                      | Visible text is less than a tenth of the HTML.                                                          | Move large inline code into separate files. Make sure the text is in the page source.            | low-text-ratio                            |
| Recommended properties missing in structured data                | Fields Google recommends for Article or Organization markup are missing. Rich results aren't blocked.   | Add the missing fields using information shown on the page. Not urgent.                          | structured-data-recommended-props-missing |
| No Google Analytics tag found on the pages                       | The HTML has no G-, GTM- or UA- id. If the tag loads later, ignore this finding.                        | Add the Analytics or Tag Manager code to the head section of every page.                         | analytics-tag-missing                     |
| No X-Content-Type-Options header                                 | The browser may guess file types. It doesn't affect rankings.                                           | Add "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff" to the server responses.                                   | missing-x-content-type-options            |
| Page can be embedded in other sites' frames                      | Another site can put your page in an invisible frame (clickjacking).                                    | Add a "frame-ancestors 'self'" or "X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN" header.                          | missing-clickjacking-protection           |
| No Referrer-Policy header                                        | Not urgent. The header decides how much of your address is shared when visitors leave for another site. | Add a "Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin" header.                                 | missing-referrer-policy                   |
| No SPF record on the domain                                      | Others can send fake email in your name. It doesn't affect SEO directly.                                | Add the SPF record your email provider recommends to DNS as a TXT record.                        | missing-spf                               |
| No DMARC record on the domain                                    | Nothing says what to do with email that fails verification. It doesn't affect SEO directly.             | Add a TXT record named \_dmarc to DNS. Start with p=none.                                        | missing-dmarc                             |

## Additional checks

These rules come from the Lighthouse report of the speed measurement, from the page HTML and from the optional outgoing-link and image checks. The Severity column shows which group each rule counts in.

| Rule                                                           | Severity | What it means                                                                                                           | How to fix                                                | ID                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Files are blocking the page's first render                     | Warning  | CSS and scripts delay the first render.                                                                                 | Add defer to scripts the first screen doesn't need.       | lh-render-blocking          |
| The page loads JavaScript it doesn't use                       | Warning  | JavaScript that never runs is downloaded.                                                                               | Remove unused plugins and tags.                           | lh-unused-javascript        |
| Images are downloaded larger than they need to be              | Warning  | Image files are larger than their displayed size or format needs, which slows loading.                                  | Convert to WebP/AVIF, compress and resize.                | lh-image-delivery           |
| The page redirects before it opens                             | Warning  | There are redirects before the page opens.                                                                              | Point links at the final address.                         | lh-document-redirects       |
| The page is sent uncompressed                                  | Warning  | HTML, CSS and JavaScript arrive without gzip or Brotli, so they take longer to download.                                | Turn on gzip or Brotli compression.                       | lh-text-compression         |
| The page's main image is marked to load late                   | Warning  | The main image has loading="lazy".                                                                                      | Remove lazy from the main image on the first screen.      | lh-lcp-lazy-loaded          |
| Some text has too little color contrast                        | Warning  | Text doesn't stand out enough from its background.                                                                      | Ensure at least 4.5:1 contrast.                           | lh-a11y-color-contrast      |
| Images are missing alternative text (Lighthouse)               | Warning  | The rendered page has images without alt text, so screen readers and Google cannot tell what they show.                 | Write alt text for meaningful images.                     | lh-a11y-image-alt           |
| Form fields have no label (Lighthouse)                         | Warning  | Screen readers cannot tell visitors what to enter in these fields.                                                      | Link a <label> to each field.                             | lh-a11y-label               |
| Some links have no readable name                               | Warning  | Screen readers announce these links without a name, and Google gets no hint about the target.                           | Add text or aria-label.                                   | lh-a11y-link-name           |
| Some buttons have no readable name                             | Warning  | Screen readers announce these buttons without saying what they do.                                                      | Add text or aria-label.                                   | lh-a11y-button-name         |
| The page has no title in the browser (Lighthouse)              | Warning  | The rendered page has no <title>, so browser tabs and search results have nothing to show.                              | Add a title to the HTML the server sends.                 | lh-a11y-document-title      |
| Zooming is blocked on phones (Lighthouse)                      | Warning  | Visitors cannot enlarge the text on a phone.                                                                            | Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale.                | lh-a11y-meta-viewport       |
| The page makes insecure (http) requests                        | Warning  | Some requests go to insecure http addresses. Browsers may block them or show a warning.                                 | Serve every file over https.                              | lh-is-on-https              |
| Some links can't be crawled (Lighthouse)                       | Warning  | There are links Google can't follow.                                                                                    | Give every link a real href.                              | lh-crawlable-anchors        |
| Google can't index the page (Lighthouse)                       | Warning  | Lighthouse found the page not indexable.                                                                                | Check robots.txt and noindex rules.                       | lh-is-crawlable             |
| robots.txt has invalid lines                                   | Warning  | Crawlers skip lines they cannot parse, so some of your rules may not apply.                                             | Fix lines to "Field: value" form.                         | lh-robots-txt               |
| hreflang tags are invalid (Lighthouse)                         | Warning  | Search engines ignore language versions with invalid codes or relative addresses.                                       | Use valid language codes and full addresses.              | lh-hreflang                 |
| The canonical tag is invalid (Lighthouse)                      | Warning  | The canonical has no valid address, conflicts with another canonical, or points somewhere Google will not accept.       | Keep one canonical pointing at the page's own address.    | lh-canonical                |
| Insecure image, video or frame on a secure page                | Warning  | http images, video or frames on an https page.                                                                          | Start the addresses with https.                           | mixed-content-media         |
| Form data is sent unencrypted                                  | Warning  | Form data goes to an http address.                                                                                      | Make the form's action https.                             | form-action-http            |
| The canonical tag is in the page body                          | Warning  | The canonical is in <body>; Google ignores it.                                                                          | Move the tag into <head>.                                 | canonical-outside-head      |
| Robots tags contradict each other                              | Warning  | The page carries robots instructions that disagree, such as index and noindex. Google applies the most restrictive one. | Keep a single robots tag.                                 | robots-meta-conflict        |
| The page says "not found" but answers successfully             | Warning  | The page says "not found" but returns 200.                                                                              | Return 404 or 410 if the page doesn't exist.              | page-says-not-found         |
| Placeholder text (lorem ipsum) was left on the page            | Warning  | The page has lorem ipsum placeholder text.                                                                              | Replace it with real content.                             | lorem-ipsum-text            |
| A follow-on page of a paginated list is hidden from search     | Warning  | Page 2 and later of a list are noindex.                                                                                 | Remove noindex, give each page its own canonical.         | paginated-page-noindex      |
| On a secure site, internal links go to http addresses          | Warning  | On an https site, internal links go to http.                                                                            | Write internal links with https or relative.              | internal-http-links         |
| A link to another site is broken                               | Warning  | A link to another site doesn't open.                                                                                    | Update or remove the link.                                | broken-external-link        |
| Image file is too large                                        | Warning  | An image file is over 200 KB.                                                                                           | Resize, compress, convert to WebP/AVIF.                   | image-file-too-large        |
| The page loads CSS it doesn't use                              | Info     | Style rules the page doesn't use are downloaded.                                                                        | Turn off unused stylesheets.                              | lh-unused-css               |
| JavaScript files aren't minified                               | Info     | The scripts still contain whitespace and comments that add download size.                                               | Turn on minification in your build tool or CDN.           | lh-unminified-javascript    |
| CSS files aren't minified                                      | Info     | The stylesheets still contain whitespace and comments that add download size.                                           | Turn on minification in your build tool or CDN.           | lh-unminified-css           |
| Files aren't kept in the browser long enough                   | Info     | Files have a short browser cache lifetime.                                                                              | Give unchanging files a long Cache-Control.               | lh-cache-policy             |
| The page's total download size is very large                   | Info     | The page's total size is over 2.5 MB.                                                                                   | Shrink the largest images, videos and scripts.            | lh-total-byte-weight        |
| The page structure built in the browser is very large          | Info     | The rendered page has so many elements that layout and interaction slow down.                                           | Build hidden content only when needed.                    | lh-dom-size                 |
| The server is slow to answer (Lighthouse)                      | Info     | The server's first byte takes over 600 ms.                                                                              | Turn on page caching.                                     | lh-slow-server-response     |
| Text is invisible while fonts load                             | Info     | Visitors see blank space instead of text until the web font downloads.                                                  | Add font-display: swap.                                   | lh-font-display             |
| The page's main image isn't requested with priority            | Info     | The main image is discovered late or not prioritized.                                                                   | Put it in the HTML as an <img> with fetchpriority="high". | lh-lcp-not-prioritized      |
| Files are served over old HTTP/1.1                             | Info     | Files arrive over HTTP/1.1.                                                                                             | Turn on HTTP/2 on your server or CDN.                     | lh-modern-http              |
| Unneeded JavaScript is sent for old browsers                   | Info     | Unneeded code for old browsers is sent.                                                                                 | Update your target browser setting.                       | lh-legacy-javascript        |
| Third-party code keeps the browser busy for a long time        | Info     | Third-party code holds the main thread over 0.5 s.                                                                      | Remove unneeded tags, defer the rest.                     | lh-third-parties            |
| Main content loading could be faster (LCP)                     | Info     | LCP is between 2.5 and 4 seconds.                                                                                       | Shrink the main image, turn off its lazy loading.         | cwv-lcp-needs-improvement   |
| Content shifts a little while loading (CLS)                    | Info     | CLS is between 0.1 and 0.25.                                                                                            | Give images dimensions, reserve ad space.                 | cwv-cls-needs-improvement   |
| Responses to taps could be faster (INP)                        | Info     | INP is between 200 and 500 ms (field data).                                                                             | Split long scripts that run on a click.                   | cwv-inp-needs-improvement   |
| The page's language isn't declared in the browser (Lighthouse) | Info     | No lang on the <html> element.                                                                                          | Add a language, e.g. <html lang="en">.                    | lh-a11y-html-has-lang       |
| Tap targets are too small or too close together                | Info     | Buttons and links are hard to tap accurately on a phone.                                                                | Give targets at least 24×24 pixels.                       | lh-a11y-target-size         |
| Heading order skips levels in the browser (Lighthouse)         | Info     | The rendered page jumps heading levels, for example from H2 to H4.                                                      | Use headings in order.                                    | lh-a11y-heading-order       |
| The browser logs errors while the page opens                   | Info     | Errors are logged to the console on load.                                                                               | Check the Console tab in Chrome.                          | lh-errors-in-console        |
| The page uses features browsers are removing                   | Info     | Deprecated browser features are used.                                                                                   | Update the old plugin or library.                         | lh-deprecations             |
| The browser reports problems on the page                       | Info     | Chrome's "Issues" panel logs entries.                                                                                   | Check the Issues tab in developer tools.                  | lh-inspector-issues         |
| Some images are shown at the wrong ratio                       | Info     | Images look stretched or squashed because the displayed shape differs from the file.                                    | Use the right width/height or object-fit.                 | lh-image-aspect-ratio       |
| Some images are low resolution for the screen                  | Info     | Images look blurry on high-density screens because the file is smaller than the displayed size.                         | Serve larger versions with srcset.                        | lh-image-size-responsive    |
| Link texts aren't descriptive (Lighthouse)                     | Info     | Link texts such as "click here" do not say where the link goes.                                                         | Write text about the target's topic.                      | lh-link-text                |
| The page redirects with meta refresh                           | Info     | The page forwards visitors with a meta refresh tag instead of a server redirect.                                        | Redirect on the server (301).                             | meta-refresh-redirect       |
| The canonical address is written as relative                   | Info     | The canonical is a relative path, which can resolve to the wrong address.                                               | Write a full address (https://...).                       | canonical-relative          |
| The canonical address has a # fragment                         | Info     | Google ignores everything after #, so the canonical may not point where you intend.                                     | Remove the # and what follows.                            | canonical-with-fragment     |
| Search doesn't show the page's snippet                         | Info     | nosnippet or max-snippet:0 hides the snippet.                                                                           | Remove the rule if it's not intentional.                  | snippet-blocked             |
| An e-mail address is exposed as plain text                     | Info     | Spam bots collect e-mail addresses written in plain text.                                                               | Consider a contact form.                                  | exposed-email-address       |
| The title's words don't appear in the page content             | Info     | The main words of the title are missing from the page text, so the title may promise something the page does not cover. | Write the title around the page's topic.                  | title-content-mismatch      |
| Organization structured data lists no social profiles          | Info     | Organization markup has no sameAs links to your official profiles, which help Google connect them to your brand.        | Add official profile addresses to sameAs.                 | organization-missing-sameas |
| A deep page has no breadcrumb trail                            | Info     | A page several levels deep has no breadcrumb trail, so visitors and Google see less of the site structure.              | Add a breadcrumb trail and BreadcrumbList.                | missing-breadcrumbs         |
| The code embedded in the page is very large                    | Info     | Inline script and style exceed 100 KB.                                                                                  | Move large inline code into files.                        | large-inline-code           |
| There's a blog but no RSS/Atom feed is declared                | Info     | The site has blog posts but declares no RSS or Atom feed for readers and feed services.                                 | Declare the feed with <link rel="alternate">.             | missing-feed                |

## How the rules run

**Per-page rules** check each crawled page and list every page they affect.

**Site-wide rules** produce one finding for the whole site. The robots.txt and sitemap rules work this way, as do "Site has no social sharing tags (Open Graph)" and "Site has no structured data". A second group probes the site once at the start of the audit: www and non-www addresses, the http-to-https redirect, the response to a random address that does not exist, robots.txt blocking the whole site, its Sitemap line and AI crawlers, the site icon, llms.txt, security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy), and the start page's size, compression and time to first byte.

**External sources.** The SSL certificate's expiry date comes from public Certificate Transparency logs, the domain's expiry date from registration data (RDAP), and the SPF and DMARC records from DNS. "Analytics id on the pages doesn't match the connected property" compares the measurement ID found in the HTML with the web streams of the GA4 property connected to the project.

**Google rules.** Rules whose name starts with "Google" use the answers stored on the **Index status** tab, not the crawl. They run only after you have checked pages on that tab.

**Speed rules.** The LCP, CLS and INP rules, the Lighthouse SEO score and every rule whose ID starts with `lh-` read the Lighthouse report that PageSpeed Insights returns for each page. They run only when **Also measure page speed** is on, and they use the mobile measurement. A Lighthouse check that did not run or failed on a page counts as neither a finding nor a pass.

**Outgoing links and image sizes.** "A link to another site is broken" and "Image file is too large" run only when **Also check outgoing links and image sizes** is on. After the crawl, the audit requests at most 300 such addresses. Sites that block bots, such as social networks, and addresses that do not respond are never counted as broken.

A rule that an audit did not measure shows as **Not measured** on the **Checks** tab. This includes audits that ran before the rule existed.

---

# Agent setup

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/agent-setup/

> Connect Claude Code, Codex or another MCP client to seowatcher, confirm it with a fresh tool call and install the six SEO skills.

seowatcher exposes its data to AI assistants over MCP (Model Context Protocol). A connected assistant can read your Search Console, Analytics and audit data, start audits and save reports. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and any other client that supports MCP. Anything the assistant reads can be sent to that assistant's provider.

## Connect your agent

1. Open **Agent setup** in the app.
2. Under **Which agent do you use?**, choose **Claude Code**, **Codex** or **Other**. Arrow keys, Home and End move between the options without copying anything.
3. Select **Copy setup command** and paste the command into your agent.

The agent connects seowatcher, installs the SEO skills and walks you through any step you must do by hand. The command contains no token: the agent reads the local token from your computer instead of writing it into the chat.

If you have just installed seowatcher and nothing is configured yet, use **Fresh install** instead. That command has the agent check the install, the Google connection, the PageSpeed key and your first project before it connects itself.

## Confirm the connection

Select **Verify connection**, then ask your agent to call any seowatcher tool. The page checks for a new call every five seconds for up to 60 seconds. A call made before you started verifying does not count. Checking stops if you switch tabs, cancel or a read fails.

If no new call arrives, check your client's MCP status and try again. A timeout does not prove that the connection is broken.

The connected and last-call dates describe past use, not a live session. An assistant's access covers the whole installation, not only the project open in the browser.

## Skills

The **Skills** tab lists the six SEO workflows the setup command installs, such as `seo-audit` and `seo-report`. Call them as `/seo-audit` in Claude Code or `$seo-audit` in Codex. To refresh skills you installed earlier, use **Copy update command**; your connection settings and your own edits stay as they are.

## Manual setup and the token

Use the setup command when you can. For a manual setup, put the token only in your client's local header field: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. These PowerShell commands copy it to the clipboard without printing it.

Windows package:

`(Get-Content "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\seowatcher\mcp-token").Trim() | Set-Clipboard`

Docker:

`(docker compose exec -T seotracker cat /app/.wrangler/mcp-token).Trim() | Set-Clipboard`

After pasting, clear the clipboard. Never put the token in a chat, terminal output, screenshot or source code. On Windows, **Veri klasörünü aç** (Open data folder) in the tray menu opens the folder that holds the token file.

## If the agent cannot connect

- **401 Unauthorized**: the client is not sending the `Authorization` header, or the token is wrong.
- **Connection refused**: seowatcher is not running, or the client points to the wrong address or port.

After fixing either one, reconnect MCP in your client and verify with a new tool call. See [Troubleshooting](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/troubleshooting/) for more detail.

---

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/troubleshooting/

> Symptom, cause and fix for the problems users hit most: port conflicts, Windows warnings, Google errors, quotas, audits and agent access.

Start with the **App health** card on the [Help](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/help/) screen. It checks sign-in and access, Google sign-in, the PageSpeed key, the runtime and the database, and links each problem to the setting that fixes it. The sections below run from the most common problem to the rarest. Tray menu items are in Turkish only, so they are given in Turkish with the English meaning in brackets.

## The page does not open

**Symptom:** The browser says "connection refused".

**Cause:** The app is not running.

**Fix (Windows package):** Look for the seowatcher icon in the notification area; click the ^ arrow on the taskbar if it is hidden. If there is no icon, open seowatcher from the Start menu. Hovering over the icon should show "Çalışıyor: http://127.0.0.1:3001/" (Running); if the port number is different, open that address. If it says "Hata" (Error), right-click it and choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart), or if that does not help, **Kurulumu onar** (Repair installation). **Günlükleri aç** (Open logs) shows the reason in the last lines of `launcher.log` and `server.log`.

**Fix (Docker):** First check that Docker Desktop is running. In the project folder, run `docker compose ps`. If the status is not healthy, run `docker compose up -d`; `docker compose logs --tail 50` shows the reason.

## The port number is in use

**Symptom:** On Windows, a yellow strip appears at the top of every screen in the app: "seowatcher is running on 3002 this time because another program is using 3001 (for example an old Docker copy). Google sign-in is set up for 3001; close that program and restart seowatcher." Connecting to Google gives an error. Or the icon says "3001 ve sonraki 9 adres numarası (port) dolu" (3001 and the next 9 ports are in use). The same sentence is written in the "App health" card on the **Help** screen. On Docker, you see "Bind for 127.0.0.1:3001 failed".

**Cause:** Another program is using the same port number. The most common cause is an old Docker copy you once ran. Docker Desktop can restart it by itself when the computer starts. Google's redirect addresses name 3001, so Google sign-in does not work while the app is open on 3002.

**Fix:** The Windows package normally picks a free number between 3002 and 3010, tells you in a balloon and in the strip above, and uses it only for that one start. First close the program that holds 3001. If it is an old Docker copy, stop the seotracker container in Docker Desktop, or run `docker compose stop` in the project folder. Then choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the menu. The app returns to 3001 and the strip disappears. Closing the strip only hides it for that tab; it does not fix anything. If they are all in use, write a different number in the `config.json` file in the data folder. On Docker, create a `.env` file with the line `PORT=3002` and run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate seotracker`. When the number changes, update the Google redirect addresses too.

## The icon says "Windows bileşeni eksik"

**Symptom:** The app does not open. The icon says "Windows bileşeni eksik" (Windows component missing), or the log shows "Workers runtime failed to start" and "0xc0000005".

**Cause:** The app's engine needs Microsoft's Visual C++ package (2015-2022, 64-bit). On a clean Windows, this package is missing or out of date.

**Fix:** Click the notification that appears, or right-click the tray icon and choose **Eksik Windows bileşenini kur** (Install the missing Windows component). Windows asks for administrator permission once. When the installation finishes, the app restarts by itself. You can also download the package from Microsoft: `https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe`

## Administrator permission was refused

**Symptom:** The installer asked for permission to install Visual C++, you clicked No. The installer said "Microsoft Visual C++ çalışma zamanı kurulamadı" (The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime could not be installed).

**Cause:** The Visual C++ component was not installed. Because the app carries a copy of the files it needs, it still starts on most computers.

**Fix:** If the app started, you do not need to do anything. If it did not, choose **Eksik Windows bileşenini kur** (Install the missing Windows component) in the tray menu and allow it this time, or install the component yourself from `https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe`.

## The icon says "Uygulamanın motoru çöktü"

**Symptom:** The app does not open. The log has "Workers runtime failed to start" and "0xc0000005", but the Visual C++ package is installed.

**Cause:** The app's engine (workerd) gets stuck on a system file on this computer. At startup, the app tests the engine by itself. If that test fails too, the problem is on the computer; if it passes, the problem is in the data folder or the configuration.

**Fix:** First choose **Kurulumu onar** (Repair installation). If that does not help, right-click the icon and choose **Sorunu bildir (GitHub)** (Report the problem, GitHub). The diagnostic information (Windows version, processor, the name of the faulty module, the crash dump) is added to the report automatically, so you only need to send it. The crash dumps are in the `%LOCALAPPDATA%\seowatcher\logs\dumps` folder, and you can attach them to the report too.

## Windows says "protected your PC"

**Symptom:** The setup file does not open, and a blue warning screen appears.

**Cause:** The file is not signed. Windows shows this screen for publishers it does not know.

**Fix:** Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. To be sure, compare the file's SHA-256 digest (its fingerprint) with `SHA256SUMS.txt` on the release page.

## Google says "redirect_uri_mismatch"

**Symptom:** When you choose **Connect**, Google shows an error page.

**Cause:** The redirect address in Google Cloud Console is not exactly the same as the one in the app.

**Fix:** In the app, open **Settings → Google** and copy both redirect URIs with the copy buttons. Paste them into the OAuth client's **Authorized redirect URIs** in Google Cloud Console. Any difference matters: localhost instead of 127.0.0.1, http instead of https, or a slash at the end.

## "Google access key missing"

**Symptom:** The **Connections** tab in project settings shows a yellow "Google access key missing" warning.

**Cause:** Neither a service account (**Settings → Service account**) nor an OAuth client ID and secret (**Settings → Google**) has been saved. Or the encryption key is damaged, so the saved Google details cannot be opened.

**Fix:** Save a service account or an OAuth client (see [Connecting to Google](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/google-connection/)). One of them is enough; if both are saved, the service account is used. The "Google sign-in" row on the **Help** screen says which one is in use.

- **Windows package:** the encryption key is the `instance-secret` file in the data folder, created once by the launcher. If the icon says this file is damaged, restore it from a backup; if Google was never connected, delete the file and choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart).
- **Docker:** if you set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` by hand, it must be at least 32 characters. If you leave it empty, the container creates one itself.

## Google says "access_denied"

**Symptom:** After Google's permission screen, the app says "Google sign-in was canceled".

**Cause:** The Google account you signed in with is not in the test users list on the consent screen.

**Fix:** In Cloud Console, add the account under **OAuth consent screen → Test users**. Then choose **Connect** again.

## The connection has expired

**Symptom:** The integration card says "The connection has expired" and no data comes in.

**Cause:** For apps in "Test" status, Google can expire the permission after seven days. The encryption key may also have changed.

**Fix:** On the card, choose **Reconnect**. If it keeps happening, move the consent screen to production, or switch to a service account (**Settings → Service account**).

## There is no query data and the charts are empty

**Symptom:** The **Dashboard** cards show zero. Search performance says "No data for this period yet".

**Cause:** There are three possible causes: the site is new and Google has not shown it yet; Search Console is three days behind and the selected period is too short; or the wrong property is selected.

**Fix:** Set the period to **Last 3 months**. In the project settings, check that the property is the right site. A domain property covers all subdomains, but a URL-prefix property does not. On a new site, query rows can take weeks to arrive. The page table fills earlier.

## The table total does not match the card

**Symptom:** When you add up the impressions in the page table, the result is larger than the number on the card.

**Cause:** This is not a bug. Google counts each page that appears in the same search separately. The card is the site total.

**Fix:** Read the total from the card. Read the table page by page.

## An audit is stuck on "In progress"

**Symptom:** There has been no progress for half an hour.

**Cause:** The app may have restarted, or the job may have dropped.

**Fix:** Wait. The app checks any audit that has shown "In progress" for more than 15 minutes. If there are no signs of life, it closes the audit as "Failed" and records the reason. Then choose **Run again with the same settings**. Do not start two audits with speed testing at the same time. They slow each other down.

## The audit says "The audit stopped before it could finish"

**Symptom:** The audit screen says "The audit stopped during the crawl phase." or "The audit stopped before it could finish." Instead of the score, it says "Incomplete audit — no score given".

**Cause:** The screen says three things: what happened, whether the fault is in your site or in the app, and what to do. The title says in which phase it stopped: URL discovery, crawl, speed test or results preparation.

**Fix:** Follow the sentence on the screen.

- **A step did not finish in time.** Usually the site is answering very slowly. Try again in a few minutes. If it happens again, start with fewer pages.
- **The audit did not fit in the memory**, **went over the processor time**, or **the result of one step was larger than the app can store.** Very large or complex pages cause this. Start again with fewer pages.
- **An error occurred while writing the results to the database.** The disk may be full or the data file may be locked by another program. Check that the disk has free space, restart the app, then start the audit again.
- **The app's internal audit engine reported an error.** Choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the tray menu, then start the audit again.
- **The audit was cut off.** The app may have been closed or restarted in the middle of it. Make sure the app stays open and start the audit again.
- **The install key did not reach the part that runs audits.** Your saved Google and PageSpeed keys were not deleted. Update or restart the app, then start the audit again.
- **An unexpected error.** Start the audit again. If it keeps happening, download the diagnostics bundle from the **Help** screen and report the problem.

The raw error text does not reach the screen. It stays in the diagnostics bundle.

## The audit says "Partial score"

**Symptom:** The score has no rating word beside it. A line like "Partial score — measurement coverage 62%" is there.

**Cause:** A large share of the checks could not be measured (the share of measured checks is below 70 percent, or fewer than half the checks in Crawling, Indexing, Content or Speed were measured). The lines under the card give the reasons: the PageSpeed quota ran out, there is no PageSpeed key, speed testing was turned off, or no index data could be fetched from Search Console.

**Fix:** Turn on speed measurement, add a PageSpeed key or connect Search Console, then run the audit again. The score is based on what was measured. No judgement, good or bad, was made about the rest.

## The audit says "Incomplete audit — no score given"

**Symptom:** This sentence sits where the score card would be. The findings are still shown below it.

**Cause:** The audit stopped with an error, is still running, or the crawl stopped early because of the site's rate limit. The issue list is incomplete, so no score was calculated. If no page could be crawled, the score card does not appear at all.

**Fix:** Read the reason in the section above. Run the audit again once the rate limit has reset or the problem is fixed. The findings apply to the pages that were crawled.

## The audit finished but says "the speed test ran without a key"

**Symptom:** The audit completed. A warning says "The saved PageSpeed key could not be read, so the speed test ran without a key." The Speed tab has at most 50 pages.

**Cause:** The part that runs audits did not receive the install key that opens the saved key, so the speed test ran without it. The crawl results were not affected.

**Fix:** Update or restart the app, then start a new audit. If it continues, save the PageSpeed key again in **Settings**.

## The audit says it was blocked

**Symptom:** A yellow warning says "The audit could not fully crawl this site." or "We were blocked on N pages."

**Cause:** The site's bot protection (Cloudflare or a firewall) stopped the app's site crawler.

**Fix:** In the firewall, allow the user agent named `seotracker-audit`, or add your computer's network address (IP) to the allow list. If the site is not yours, you cannot fix this. The results stay limited to the pages that could be crawled.

## Speed testing is incomplete or missing

**Symptom:** The Speed tab is empty or has very few rows. The quota card says "Quota used up", a per-minute limit message or "No key".

**Cause:** There is no PageSpeed key (at most 50 pages are measured). Or Google's daily allowance has run out.

**Fix:** Add a free key; see [PageSpeed key](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/pagespeed-key/). If the daily allowance has run out, a new audit tomorrow completes the measurement. If speed testing was off when an audit started, that audit is never measured afterwards.

## URL Inspection says "daily limit reached"

**Symptom:** On the **Index status** tab, **Check status on Google** is disabled and the tab says "Google's daily limit of 2,000 URLs is used up".

**Cause:** Google allows 2,000 questions per day per property. The app, your assistant and the checks you make by hand in Search Console all use the same pool.

**Fix:** The limit counts the last 24 hours, so the allowance frees up gradually within hours; continue then. The app only asks again for answers that have gone stale, so your allowance is not wasted.

## The Analytics card or report shows an error

**Symptom:** The **Organic traffic** card on the **Dashboard**, or the Analytics screen, shows a sentence instead of data, with **Fix the connection** and **Try again** buttons.

**Cause:** The sentence gives the cause and the fix. The main cases are these.

- **The connection has expired or was revoked.** Connect it again in **Settings**.
- **Access to this property was refused (HTTP 403).** Give the connected account or service account at least the Viewer role on the property.
- **The property was not found (HTTP 404).** It may have been deleted or moved. Choose it again in **Settings**.
- **No property is connected to this project.** Choose one in **Settings**.
- **The reporting quota is used up (HTTP 429).** The quota refreshes hourly and daily. Try again later.
- **The Google Analytics Data API is off in the Google Cloud project.** Turn on "Google Analytics Data API" in Google Cloud Console and try again.
- **The report is not compatible with the selected property (HTTP 400).** Check the property or choose another.
- **Google returned an invalid answer or is not answering for the moment.** Try again shortly.
- **Google cannot be reached.** Check this computer's internet connection.

**Fix:** Do the step the sentence names. Most often **Fix the connection** takes you to the right setting.

## A Search Console request shows an error

**Symptom:** Search performance, Opportunities or Rank tracking shows a Search Console error instead of data.

**Cause:** The error sentence names the cause.

- **The request was found invalid (HTTP 400).** This is not a connection problem. The chosen dimension, filter or search type cannot be used on this property. Remove the filters.
- **Access to the property was refused (HTTP 401 or 403).** Check that the account has verified permission on the property, or refresh the connection in **Settings**.
- **The property was not found (HTTP 404).** It may have been removed from Search Console. Choose it again in **Settings**.
- **The request limit is used up (HTTP 429).** Try again in a few minutes.
- **It did not answer in time.** Try again shortly.
- **It is not answering for the moment (another HTTP code).** Try again shortly. If it continues, look at Google's status page.
- **Google cannot be reached.** The sentence gives a detail on the "Reason" line. If it continues, check this computer's internet connection.

**Fix:** Do the step the sentence names. For account and property problems, refreshing the connection in **Settings** is usually enough.

## Localhost traffic shows up in Analytics

**Symptom:** In the landing pages table, the Domain column shows localhost or 127.0.0.1.

**Cause:** A test copy of your site loads the same Analytics tag.

**Fix:** Set the tag to load only on the real domain. Most tools have a "domain check" option. The app does not filter these rows out, so until you fix the tag, read the table with the **Domain** column in view.

## The assistant cannot connect (401)

**Symptom:** Claude Code or Codex says "Unauthorized".

**Cause:** The client is not sending the token, or the token is wrong.

**Fix:** Use **Copy setup command** on the **Agent setup** screen. The command detects your install type and puts the token into your tool's settings without printing it. To set it by hand, read the token again as shown below, and never paste it into a chat or screenshot.

- **Windows package:** the token is in the file `%LOCALAPPDATA%\seowatcher\mcp-token` (menu: **Veri klasörünü aç**, Open data folder). The launcher creates it on first start and hands it to the app at every start. To copy it to the clipboard without printing it, in PowerShell: `(Get-Content "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\seowatcher\mcp-token").Trim() | Set-Clipboard`. Clear the clipboard after pasting (Win+V, Clear all). There is no `docker` command on this install.
- **Docker:** the token is inside the container: `docker compose exec -T seotracker cat /app/.wrangler/mcp-token`. In Git Bash, put `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` in front, or the output comes back empty. Leave out the line break at the end of the value. You can set your own token with `MCP_TOKEN` in `.env`; after changing it, run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate seotracker`.

Then, in Claude Code, type `/mcp` and choose **Reconnect**.

## I changed a setting and the app does not see it

**Symptom:** A new port number, `.env` value or token has not reached the app.

**Cause:** What you enter on the Settings screen (Google, service account, PageSpeed key, language) applies immediately. Settings in files are read only at the next start, and the two installs keep them in different files.

**Fix (Windows package):** There is no `.env` and there are no environment variables. The only file you edit by hand is `config.json` in the data folder: `"port"` and `"autoUpdate"`. After changing it, choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the menu. Do not edit the `server.env` file next to it; the launcher rewrites it at every start.

**Fix (Docker):** The variables are in the `.env` file in the project folder (list: `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`). After changing it, recreate the container: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate seotracker`. A plain `docker compose restart seotracker` only restarts it and does not apply a `.env` change.

## Docker takes very long on first start or is "unhealthy"

**Symptom:** `docker compose ps` still does not say healthy after five minutes.

**Cause:** On first start, the app is built inside the container and needs about 2 GB of memory. If memory is not enough, the build fails.

**Fix:** Run `docker compose logs --tail 50` and check the last lines. If there is a memory error, give the containers more memory in the Docker Desktop settings. Then run `docker compose up -d --build`.

## Where are my data and logs?

On Windows, everything is in the `%LOCALAPPDATA%\seowatcher` folder: `data` (the database), `logs\launcher.log`, `logs\server.log`, `logs\migrate.log`, `instance-secret`, `mcp-token`, `config.json`. When a log file grows too large (`server.log` 5 MB, the others 1 MB), the old one stays beside it under a name like `server.old.log` and a new one starts from the beginning. The `logs\wrangler` folder holds the engine's own detailed logs; files older than 30 days are deleted automatically. **Open logs** and **Open data folder** in the taskbar menu take you there.

On Docker, the data is in the `seotracker_data` volume (`/app/.wrangler`). You see the logs with the `docker compose logs -f` command.

When you report a problem, press **Download diagnostics bundle** on the **Help** screen. The package includes phase and error summaries for the last 25 audits; page URLs are removed from PageSpeed error text. It may contain identifying details such as project names and domains, so review it before attaching it to a GitHub issue.

## A Windows setting cannot be saved

**Symptom:** Changing an option in the Windows section of **Settings** gives an error, or the section says Windows preferences are unavailable.

**Cause:** This section talks to the app in the taskbar. The error sentence says which of these it is.

- **The tray app did not answer within 4 seconds.** If the computer just woke from sleep, press **Try again** after a few seconds. If it persists, choose **Çıkış** (Exit) in the tray menu and open the app again.
- **Could not connect to the tray app's settings service.** The tray app may have closed. Open seowatcher again from the Start menu.
- **This preference is locked by an administrator.** Only the computer's administrator can change it.
- **The tray app did not recognise this request.** The server and the tray app may be left over from different sessions. Choose **Çıkış** (Exit) in the tray menu and open the app again.
- **The tray app refused the settings request.** Restart the app from the tray menu. If it persists, update the Windows package.
- **The tray app returned an unrecognised answer.** The app and tray versions may not match. Update the Windows package.

**Fix:** Do the step the sentence names. These options exist only in the Windows package. On Docker, you manage startup behaviour from your operating system.

## Launcher messages

These messages appear on the Windows icon or in a dialog. The Windows launcher is the small program that starts the app.

- **"Sunucu 120 saniyede yanıt vermedi"** (The server did not answer within 120 seconds): choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart). If that fails, choose **Günlükleri aç** (Open logs) and read `server.log`.
- **"seowatcher yeniden başlatılıyor"** (seowatcher is restarting): the server closed by itself and the app is reopening it. Refresh the open page after a few seconds.
- **"Sunucu 10 dakikada üç kez kapandı"** (The server closed three times in 10 minutes): the app has stopped reopening it. Choose **Kurulumu onar** (Repair installation), and if that does not help, **Sorunu bildir (GitHub)** (Report a problem (GitHub)).
- **"Kurulum eksik"** (Installation incomplete): **Kurulumu onar** (Repair installation) puts the missing files back by downloading the installer. If there is no internet, the releases page opens; download the installer and run it.
- **"3001 numarası dolu, 3002 kullanılıyor"** (Port 3001 is in use, using 3002): another program holds 3001, often an old Docker copy. The same warning also shows as a yellow strip across the app. If you get an error when connecting to Google, close that program and choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart). See "The port number is in use" above.
- **"Güncelleme denetlenemedi"** (The update could not be checked) or **"Güncelleme yapılamadı"** (Update failed): the balloon gives the reason. If it says "GitHub'a ulaşılamadı" (GitHub could not be reached), check your internet connection. If it says "GitHub şu an çok fazla istek alıyor" (GitHub is getting too many requests right now), try again in an hour. If the fingerprint did not match, download the installer from the releases page. In every case the installed version keeps running.
- **"Güncelleme kurulmadı"** (The update was not installed): the installer window was closed, or administrator permission was not given. Try again from **Güncelle** (Update) in the menu.
- **"Windows bileşeni kurulamadı"** (The Windows component could not be installed): choose **Eksik Windows bileşenini kur** (Install the missing Windows component) from the menu.

---

# Release notes

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/release-notes/

> seowatcher 0.8.7 Alpha (October 29, 2026): a new site audit with 202 rules, six interface languages, notifications and more accurate Google data.

The latest release is **0.8.7 Alpha**, October 29, 2026. Your data is kept when you update.

For the first move from 2.x to 0.x.x Alpha, run the new installer manually; the old updater does not recognize the lower number as newer.

## 0.8.7 Alpha — 2026-10-29

This entry brings together features and fixes from 0.5.0 to 0.8.7: site audits, the dashboard, notifications and six languages, with more accurate data and clearer screens.

### ✨ Highlights

- **Rebuilt site audit:** Checks your site page by page and as a whole against 202 rules.
- **Honest results:** Anything it cannot measure is not counted as "passed", and the screen says so when data is missing.
- **Ordered to-dos:** Problems on the pages that bring the most visitors from Google come first.
- **Six languages:** Use the app in Turkish, English, German, French, Italian or Portuguese.
- **News:** Announcements and notifications tell you about new versions and important changes.

### 🔎 Site audit

- **Security checks:** Your site's security settings and the expiry dates of its SSL certificate and domain are checked.
- **Email records:** The records that stop others from sending email in your name are checked.
- **AI crawlers:** See whether your site is open to AI crawlers such as GPTBot and ClaudeBot.
- **Speed findings:** With speed measurement on, the issues slowing your site down are listed with their estimated savings.
- **Previews:** See in advance how a page will look on Google, in shared posts and on a phone.
- **Score history:** See what improved between audits and download the updated report.

### 📊 Dashboard and reports

- **Next steps:** The dashboard has a short task list and a readiness score to help you finish your setup. The score is not an SEO result.
- **Ready-made reports:** Your AI assistant prepares an improvement report from your audit, search and Analytics data.
- **Audit progress:** While an audit runs you see the time spent and the progress, and a short summary at the end.
- **Report types:** Search reports and site audit reports are shown separately; older reports with no known type are clearly marked.
- **Report dates:** Search reports keep your selected dates and explain missing data and measurements that may change later.
- **Audit sources:** Audit reports say which traffic and speed measurements were actually used.
- **Complete Google data:** Every row Google makes available is fetched, with the time it was fetched. The ranking archive keeps filling while the page is open, and days that are not final are marked as incomplete.

### 🔔 Notifications and announcements

- **Notification center:** Audit results, new versions and Google connection problems gather in one place.
- **Notification sound:** Turn sounds for important alerts on or off in Settings.
- **Windows notifications:** Updates, announcements and finished or failed audits also appear as Windows notifications. You can turn them off in the tray icon's menu.
- **Announcements:** News from the seowatcher team appears on the app's Announcements screen.

### 🪟 Windows

- **Settings:** Choose in Settings whether the app starts with Windows and updates itself.
- **Startup progress:** A window shows the percentage while the app gets ready and while an update downloads.
- **Clear guidance:** The guide and Help explain the differences between the Windows package and Docker.

### 🌍 Languages

- **Language choice:** Pick your language under Settings → Appearance; numbers and dates follow it.
- **Guide:** The user guide, audit rules and release notes are available in six languages.
- **Privacy:** On seowatcher.io, measurement runs only if you accept it.
- **Reviewed translations:** Screen text and guides in all six languages were updated to match the revised screens.
- **Translation fixes:** Mistranslated column and category names on the French, German, Italian and Portuguese screens were corrected; the Analytics role is now named "Viewer", as in Google.

### 🎨 Appearance and help

- **Light theme:** A warmer gray background, lighter cards and a stronger orange accent improve contrast.
- **Cards and numbers:** Summary cards are simpler, and changing numbers respect your reduced-motion preference.
- **Help and notes:** Help and release notes make it easier to find the information you need.
- **Data colors:** Clicks are blue, impressions violet, CTR teal, position ochre, sessions green and conversions rose. Cards and charts use the same colors in both themes.
- **Calmer screens:** Source, period and freshness appear together with short labels, and longer explanations open on request. Shorter names and clearer buttons make actions easier to find.
- **On phones:** Lists show as readable rows instead of tables, and query names and labels are no longer cut off.
- **One look:** Buttons, expandable sections, notification pop-ups and cards look the same on every screen; single-page lists no longer show page buttons.

### 🗂️ Projects and saved searches

- **Saved keywords:** Positions are calculated for your saved list, spelling variants no longer overwrite each other, and unknown positions are clearly marked.
- **Project summary:** Missing archive days no longer count as lost traffic; the audit summary only shows your project's site.
- **Project context:** When edits conflict, you keep your draft and can compare it with the latest text.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **More accurate audits:** Errors found on real sites were fixed; comparisons use each audit’s own pages, and an audit record is kept if startup fails. Failure messages in the audit history fit the screen, and its counts state that they include both page and site-wide findings.
- **Menus and keyboard:** Screens, reports and country lists fit on phones; menus stay on screen, keyboard focus stays in the open window, and Esc closes only the top list while keeping your text; screen readers announce selections, and Analytics shows channel names in your language. On phones, the update time, report type and labels on every Rank tracking row are visible.
- **Everyday fixes:** The diagnostics bundle in Help describes problems better and leaves out your page addresses. 25 issues found with real data were fixed across the dashboard, Search performance, Rank tracking, Saved keywords, Analytics, Reports, Site audit, Settings, connections and Help. Every screen was reviewed twice more with real data, including the bottom of each page. Dashboard audit counts say what they count, and issue names appear in full. An empty saved-keyword list says so immediately. Rank tracking describes positions as averages for the selected period, Help uses the name Project context, and page controls read Previous page and Next page. The dashboard's sessions chart has the correct label. Singular and plural wording was corrected in English, German, French, Italian and Portuguese. Your AI assistant can again find pages competing for the same query.
- **More accurate numbers:** Missing measurements are not counted as zero, and limited Analytics data is not presented as a firm conclusion. Rankings use matching dates, priority tasks and estimate limits are explained, and filtering no longer changes estimated monthly gains. Opportunities explains the queries Google hides and no longer suggests widening to 90 days when 90 days is already selected. On sites with few visitors, missing data is kept apart from a real zero, and Opportunities still lists pages with their measured figures. Analytics explains an unknown measurement once, and empty tables hide the page buttons. When a suggestion is based on average position alone and no gain can be calculated, the gain is shown as unknown.
- **Connection status:** A selected property is no longer shown as verified access, and old results are not treated as current after an account change. Unresponsive Google requests time out, temporary errors suggest trying again, and disabled APIs say what to enable.
- **Saved data:** Adding or removing tags always completes in full, tags in use cannot be deleted, historical data stays tied to the right property, and queued tasks run in the right order.
- **Windows startup:** Working files are stored in your user folder, repaired assistant connections survive a restart, and the startup check no longer hangs. A Windows settings link that could not work is hidden. Notifications that arrived while you were away appear when you return to the app.

### 🔒 Security

- **Up-to-date components:** Known vulnerabilities in the app's dependencies were fixed.
- **Secret keys:** The Google service account file can be saved without its contents appearing on screen.
- **Assistant setup:** Setup instructions never ask you to print your token or paste it into a chat.

## 0.4.3 Alpha — 2026-10-23

One-click installation arrived for Windows, and the seowatcher.io website and user guide went live.

### ✨ Highlights

- **One-click install:** Install on Windows with a single file, without Docker or a terminal.
- **Updates itself:** The app downloads, verifies and installs new versions.
- **Website and guide:** seowatcher.io and the user guide are live in six languages.

### 🪟 Windows

- **Easy install:** Run the file; it prepares everything needed and opens the browser. Uninstalling does not delete your data.
- **Taskbar:** Manage the app from its taskbar icon.
- **Updating:** The Update option shows progress; if you like, updates install by themselves.
- **Recovers itself:** If the app closes unexpectedly it restarts, and log files no longer grow without limit.
- **Repair and report:** Repair installation fixes startup problems, and Report a problem opens a pre-filled issue with your personal details removed.

### 🧭 First setup

- **Start from scratch:** On Agent setup, Fresh install is at the top and needs only one copy button.
- **Google connection:** Settings explains it in three short steps.
- **Clear feedback:** Saving, deleting and connecting tell you what happened; deleting asks first.

### 🌐 Website and guide

- **seowatcher.io:** The app's website is live in six languages.
- **User guide:** A 20-page guide you can read in six languages.
- **Troubleshooting:** Each problem is described by symptom, cause and fix.

### 🎨 Look and feel

- **Simpler screens:** The menu, settings and first-setup screens were simplified.
- **Natural wording:** More than two hundred screen texts were rewritten.
- **Dark theme:** Dark is the default theme; light and dark both match the website.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **Google connection:** A wrong "access key missing" warning that appeared only with a service-account connection is gone.
- **Analytics:** Device, channel and country names are shown in your language; revenue shows its currency; change percentages look the same everywhere.
- **Phone layout:** The Site audit and Opportunities screens no longer overflow on a phone.

## 0.2.1 Alpha — 2026-10-04

The first release of seowatcher: it gathers your Google data, site audit and speed tests in one app on your own computer.

### ✨ Highlights

- **Data in one place:** Search Console, Analytics, the site audit and speed tests in one app.
- **Site audit:** See your site's problems, the pages they affect and the audit history.
- **Reports:** Download and print the audit report.

### 📈 Search performance

- **Search tracking:** Follow your performance on Google and the rankings of your saved keywords.
- **Opportunities:** Lists the improvements most likely to lift your rankings.
- **Clear limits:** Your remaining daily Google quota and speed tests are shown on screen.

### 🤖 AI assistant

- **Easy setup:** Paste the setup prompt into your AI assistant and it checks the rest.
- **No secrets in chat:** It never asks you to paste passwords into the chat.
- **Codex support:** Codex has its own one-command guide.

### 🎨 Look and accessibility

- **Light and dark theme:** Pick the theme that suits your eyes.
- **Accessibility:** Works with a keyboard and a screen reader.
- **Live progress:** Audit progress shows an estimate of the time left; no animation plays if reduced motion is on.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **Stuck audits:** An audit that stopped partway no longer blocks a new one.
- **More accurate results:** Page depth, sitemap coverage and orphan pages are calculated more accurately; http, https and www differences now show up.
- **Google account:** When the account or property changes, an old project's data no longer gets mixed in.
- **Connection time:** You are no longer asked to reconnect after about an hour.

### 🔒 Security

- **Safe reports:** Downloaded reports are protected against content from maliciously crafted pages.

## Version numbers

seowatcher uses 0.x Alpha numbers until 1.0. A new feature you can notice raises the middle number (0.7.1 → 0.8.0); a fix-only release raises the last number (0.8.0 → 0.8.2). A new entry is added only for a milestone users will notice; small fixes go into the current entry, which takes the newest number. The releases from 0.0.0 to 0.4.3 were first published with v2.x tags; the matching table is at the top of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ucsahinn/seotracker/blob/seotracker-fork/CHANGELOG.md).

The full history is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ucsahinn/seotracker/blob/seotracker-fork/CHANGELOG.md) on GitHub.
